jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Product Partnerships at Ramp is where we go when the right partner doesn't exist yet — or when the canonical partner doesn't move fast enough. The team owns the integrations that expand Ramp's product surface area: tax and compliance automation, agentic commerce, data partnerships, international payments, receipt and payment automation, and the technical substrate that lets Ramp plug into any system a customer runs.

This role isn't about hitting a quota. It's about picking the right partners in emerging categories, negotiating the terms, shipping the integration with our Product and Engineering teams, and turning the launch into something customers actually feel. Recent and active examples: selecting an AI-native VAT compliance partner, white-labeling eInvoicing for international markets, shipping receipt automation, building agentic payment partnerships, and negotiating data governance terms with the largest platforms in the industry.

You'll work directly with Product, Engineering, Legal, and GTM. You'll own deals end-to-end. The bar is partnerships that move Ramp's product forward — not deals that move a number on a dashboard.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full lifecycle of strategic product partnerships: source, qualify, negotiate commercial and legal terms, structure the integration with Product and Engineering, launch, and scale

  • Translate partner capabilities into product opportunities: work side-by-side with Product and Engineering to scope what's worth building, and with Legal on risk, liability, and regulatory framing

  • Negotiate complex commercial terms — pricing, rev share, MSA, BAFO cycles, multi-year structure, data and IP rights

  • Quarterback launches across Marketing, Sales, and Solutions to make sure customers actually adopt what we ship

  • Build durable relationships with senior counterparts at partner organizations and run formal cadences (QBRs, exec syncs) once partnerships are live

  • Define and report against partnership KPIs that map to Ramp's product and revenue priorities

What You Need

  • 7+ years across Business Development, Strategic Partnerships, Product Partnerships, Product Management, or a related discipline, with a clear track record of owning deals end to end (sourcing through launch)

  • Experience structuring and closing partnerships that required real product and engineering work — not channel referrals or reseller motions

  • Strong fluency with API-based integrations: comfortable scoping technical work directly with engineers and PMs, and translating between partner-side and product-side stakeholders

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity — you've picked partners in spaces where there was no obvious incumbent and made the call stick

  • Strong commercial instincts: pricing, term structure, risk allocation, and the ability to drive a contract to signature without hand-holding from legal

Nice to Haves

  • Background that includes one of the categories above. Strong preference for Product Management

  • Direct experience negotiating data, API, or model-access governance terms (MCP, model providers, platform data exposure)

  • Shipped a product partnership that opened a new vertical, geography, or category for your company

  • Prior exposure to ERP or accounting ecosystems (relevant context, not the primary job)

  • Experience as a design-partner manager for early-stage products

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

The next chapter for this team is to build marketing-led products: intelligent tools that turn strategy into execution, automate complex workflows, and help teams operate across channels with dramatically more leverage.

The team will build across creative production, lifecycle marketing, paid media, account-based marketing, experimentation, incentives, and cross-channel orchestration. Examples include AI-powered systems that produce on-brand campaign assets, automate complex marketing workflows, coordinate audiences and execution, and deliver personalized experiences across email, sales outreach, external channels, and Ramp’s product.

A core part of this mandate is Ramp’s incentives platform. We are building shared infrastructure to safely target, authorize, distribute, redeem, and measure incentives across channels and mediums—including in-app experiences tied to product adoption and growth goals. This requires combining marketer-friendly workflows with governed policies, budget controls, reliable financial operations, and closed-loop measurement.

You will work at the intersection of product engineering, AI, data, marketing, and financial infrastructure. The ideal candidate is a product-minded backend engineer who can translate ambiguous workflows into durable systems. You will build the data models, APIs, integrations, and orchestration capabilities that allow marketers, product teams, and AI agents to safely execute complex work end to end.

What You’ll Do

  • Build the backend systems that power AI-native marketing and growth products across creative production, experimentation, incentives, and cross-channel orchestration.

  • Build shared incentives infrastructure for eligibility, targeting, policies, budgets, authorization, issuance, redemption, and outcome tracking.

  • Enable personalized content and offers across email, sales workflows, external channels, and in-product experiences using shared customer and campaign context.

  • Design reliable orchestration for long-running work, approvals, scheduling, retries, human intervention, and safe AI or financial execution.

  • Connect marketing actions and incentive spend to measurable activation, conversion, retention, and revenue outcomes.

  • Partner across Marketing, Product Growth, Product, Data Science, Finance, and GTM Platform to own systems from early discovery through production adoption and iteration.

What You Need

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building production backend systems, with strong proficiency in Python or another modern server-side language.

  • A track record of owning production services, APIs, data models, and distributed or event-driven workflows.

  • Strong product judgment and system-design fundamentals, including data modeling, asynchronous processing, reliability, testing, and observability.

  • Experience building governed systems involving permissions, policies, budgets, balances, entitlements, or financial actions.

  • Experience applying AI to real product workflows—or strong interest in doing so—with an understanding of where deterministic controls and human approval are required.

  • Excellent cross-functional communication and a bias toward rapidly shipping measurable user and business outcomes.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building incentive, rewards, promotion, loyalty, payments, ledger, or financial-authorization systems.

  • Experience building workflow engines, automation platforms, agent systems, or orchestration infrastructure.

  • Experience with lifecycle marketing, product growth, paid media, experimentation, CRM, or other marketing technology.

  • Experience designing human-in-the-loop AI systems, including approvals, evaluations, tool execution, and recovery.

  • Experience with customer-data platforms, identity systems, behavioral event streams, or analytical data infrastructure.

  • Experience building experimentation or attribution systems that connect interventions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

Internally, you’ll work closely with cross-functional teams to support customer initiatives, coordinate efforts, and contribute insights that help shape Ramp’s product and operational processes.

  • Lead customer conversations across all seniority levels, including operators, finance leadership, and C-suite executives, to ensure alignment and drive strong business outcomes

  • Manage renewals end-to-end, from identifying the need to solution design, positioning, and negotiation

  • Create and execute scalable account plans, highlighting areas of risk, opportunity, and long-term strategy

  • Run regular touchpoints — status calls, optimization reviews, roadmap conversations, and QBRs — to keep customers engaged and successful

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Support, CSMs, and Solutions teams to deliver a cohesive and high-quality customer experience

  • Travel occasionally for customer on-sites, events, and internal summits

  • Strong familiarity with Fintech, Payments, Finance/Accounting, or B2B SaaS

  • Comfortable explaining product workflows, integrations, and technical requirements to both financial and technical stakeholders

  • Ability to articulate financial value — ROI, cost savings, operational efficiency, and modernization impacts

  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, including comfort working with senior leadership and the C-suite

  • Track record of meeting or exceeding revenue or growth targets in a fast-paced, evolving environment

  • High level of ownership, adaptability, and comfort working through ambiguity

  • Willingness to travel as needed

Nice to Haves

  • Experience in financial services sales or selling to finance teams (e.g., Office of the CFO, controllers, accounting, or expense management)

  • Experience at a high-growth startup

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Design at Ramp looks very different than it did a year ago: we’re building tools and agents, designing memory, shipping PRs, and rethinking the process every few months as new capabilities unlock. A few things have not changed, the role of design is to distill problems to their essence, obsess over craft and delight where it matters most, know customers deeply and advocate for them, lead with creativity and storytelling, and keep it fun, because a product built with joy always wins.

We're looking for a Director of Product Design to lead a team of builders across some of our highest-priority bets. This role is for you if you’re excited by:

  • Leading through craft, setting vision and unlocking customer impact: you will define where a product should go, then jump into the details with the team to unblock, teach, and ship. You raise the bar through product judgment, design craft, and your ability to make everyone around you better.

  • Actually shipping and demonstrating real impact: You'll start by owning a product area and team to build trust and get your bearings at Ramp, with room to take on broader leadership over time. You'll stay close to customers and ship meaningful work alongside your designers, product managers and engineers.

  • Building the environment where great work comes from: clear roles, high standards, low ego, and just enough structure to keep the bar high without slowing people down. That means building a caring yet demanding structure, investing deeply in people — coaching, feedback, growth — so designers can do the best work of their careers and develop in this new age of Design.

It’s never been a more interesting time to build.


Please note that this role will require you to be comfortable with working in-person at our NYC HQ (located near Madison Square Park) at least 3 days/week.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and grow a high-performing team of product designers

  • Own product vision and design direction across critical product areas

  • Partner with product and engineering to shape strategy and deliver customer impact

  • Stay close to customers and use their feedback to guide product decisions

  • Jump into the work when needed to unblock teams and accelerate progress

  • Create clarity, raise quality, and help teams ship faster

  • Raise the bar for product thinking, interaction design, systems thinking, and craft

  • Coach designers through clear feedback, high standards, and strong mentorship

  • Help define how design works in an AI-native world

  • Build strong partnerships across product, engineering, data, and design

What You Need

  • Experience leading and developing high-performing product design teams

  • Strong product judgment, design craft, and systems thinking

  • Track record of shipping products with meaningful customer and business impact

  • Deep customer empathy and comfort operating in ambiguity

  • Ability to influence across functions and develop exceptional talent

  • Curiosity that borders obsession over how AI changes the nature software and how we work

Nice to Haves

  • Founder or early-stage startup experience

  • Experience designing AI-native, automation, or agentic systems

  • Experience building workflow or operations tooling

  • Experience leading managers or multi-layered teams

  • Comfort working closely with technical teams on implementation details

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

At Ramp, people are the single biggest lever on our trajectory, and the bar for who joins this team gets higher every quarter, not lower. We're hiring a Recruiter who treats recruiting as a research discipline as much as a relationship one: someone who can map a market, identify the operators who'll outperform their peers, and run a full-cycle process that wins them.

You'll own end-to-end hiring across Sales and GTM functions, from first conversation through offer close, and partner with GTM leadership to translate ambitious hiring plans into real teams. The recruiters who do this best at Ramp combine craft on the front end (research, identification, calibration) with execution on the back end (closing, candidate experience, pipeline discipline). We're looking for both.

What You'll Do

  • Use AI and research to find top talent. You'll build target lists of high performers at peer and aspirational companies using LinkedIn Recruiter, Sales Navigator, Gong signals, internal data, and AI tools like Claude. We expect AI to be part of your daily workflow, not a novelty, but a core part of how you identify, qualify, and reach candidates.

  • Calibrate quickly and map the market. For every new search, you'll develop a clear point of view on what "great" looks like, who fits the profile, and where to find them, then share that POV with hiring managers as a written artifact rather than just a slate of resumes.

  • Run thoughtful, personalized outreach. The best replies come from outbound that's grounded in real research, a candidate's territory, deal motion, or recent move. We care more about reply rate and onsite conversion than send volume.

  • Own the full cycle, from first outreach through offer close, including pipeline hygiene in Ashby, stakeholder updates, and offer construction.

  • Close candidates with competing offers. Many of our strongest GTM hires are weighing multiple options, and you'll partner with hiring managers and leadership to build conviction, sequence references, and run a closing motion that wins on substance.

  • Be a strategic partner to GTM leaders. Push back when a search is mis-scoped, surface compensation reality early, and translate hiring-manager wishlists into a concrete profile within days.

  • Deliver an excellent candidate experience that's fair, transparent, and fast. Feedback is honest; offers move in days, not weeks.

  • Improve how we hire by contributing to process changes, comp benchmarking, employer brand, and how Ramp evaluates GTM talent.

What You Need

  • 5+ years of full-cycle GTM/Sales or G&A recruiting, ideally in a high-growth or top-tier startup environment where the bar was non-negotiable.

  • A real track record of identifying strong talent, not just running searches that closed. Bring examples of candidates you found, ran a process for, and who became top performers.

  • Comfort using AI in your day-to-day workflow. You already use LLMs to research candidates, draft personalized outreach, summarize calls, or surface signals from messy data, or you're eager to. We see AI fluency as core to how recruiting works going forward.

  • Research instincts. You can articulate why a given candidate is in the top decile of their cohort, not just that they have the right title at the right company.

  • Closing skill. You've personally closed senior hires against competing offers from top-tier companies.

  • Data literacy. You're comfortable in Ashby (or equivalent ATS) and with funnel metrics, and willing to challenge a hiring manager with the numbers when needed.

  • High urgency operating mode. You book next steps on the call, not after, and you own the candidate's experience through to signature.

  • Excellent written communication. Your outbound and your candidate updates are the work product, and they should be specific, sharp, and not template-driven.

Nice-to-Have

  • Direct experience recruiting AEs, Sales Managers, RevOps, or Sales Leadership at a high-growth fintech, SaaS, or infra company.

  • Experience building or contributing to an AI-augmented research workflow.

  • Familiarity with Ashby, LinkedIn Recruiter, Sales Navigator, and Gong.

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

About Ramp

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is building a dedicated function to drive its partnerships across the AI ecosystem — labs, AI-native companies, and the investor community — and convert those into real technical and commercial outcomes. This is a newly created, high-visibility role that sits at the intersection of strategic business development, product partnership, and ecosystem relationship-building.

Ramp is already embedded with key partners across the AI ecosystem, from working with leading labs on the latest models to serving as a design partner for emerging product capabilities. This role exists to deepen those relationships across every major lab and AI-native company, and turn them into something commercially meaningful.

There is no playbook for this.

This person will own and grow Ramp's most strategic relationships across the AI ecosystem, leading the technical side of those relationships end to end with partner product and engineering teams. The mandate spans product integrations, technical partnership strategy, deal-making, co-selling, and the creation of new revenue channels, pairing real product and engineering depth with commercial execution and ecosystem credibility.

What You'll Do

  • Demonstrate technical depth to lead AI product and integration conversations end to end with partner engineering and product teams.

  • Own Ramp's relationships with emerging labs and AI-native companies at a true partnership level — not account management

  • Be embedded in the San Francisco AI community and know who is actually driving decisions at the labs, not just what the org chart says

  • Convert ecosystem relationships into commercial outcomes — referrals, integrations, co-selling, and new revenue channels

  • Do both the business development and product/integration work, combining deal-making with genuine technical engagement

  • Stay ahead of how leading AI companies are commercializing and going to market, and help Ramp move with them — and ahead of them

  • Represent Ramp externally across the San Francisco AI community: founders, investors, lab leaders, and operators

What You'll Need

  • Deep, trusted relationships at leading AI companies with the people who make decisions and influence direction — not just formal contacts

  • Commercial outcomes tied to those relationships, including initiatives with measurable revenue potential and smarter product integrations on both sides

  • Ramp is known and respected across the San Francisco AI community as a must-know fintech partner

  • Ramp keeps pace with — and ideally stays ahead of — how quickly the labs are changing, evolving their go-to-market strategies, and commercializing

  • A repeatable business development and product motion built for the AI ecosystem, not a series of one-off partnerships

  • An ever-evolving AI partnership strategy that includes sourcing, negotiating, contracting, executing, and growing relationships with leading AI companies

Over the course of a year, success means launching public products, integrations, go-to-market initiatives, and distribution channels with labs and applied AI companies.

Near-term objectives could include inclusion in model-launch announcements and joint product-integration launches. Longer-term goals will incorporate adoption of integrations and revenue targets as distribution partnerships are executed.

Every day will look different, but the work will include meeting with cross-functional stakeholders internally and externally, keeping a pulse on applied AI and the labs, negotiating active contracts, refining and executing Ramp's AI partnership strategy, and helping Ramp get closer to the teams that matter at the top AI companies.

Nice to Haves

  • The ideal candidate combines two qualities that are hard to find in one person:

    Ecosystem connector

    • Deep personal relationships in the San Francisco AI community — founders, lab leaders, and investors — at a level where people pick up the phone

    • Experience working inside or alongside leading AI partners in a way that provides genuine credibility, not just familiarity

    • Known and trusted by the venture capital and investor community in AI

    Commercial operator

    • Has built partnerships from zero at a high-growth company and been accountable for commercial outcomes

    • Can do the product and business development work simultaneously — technically fluent enough to engage on integrations and commercially sharp enough to close deals

    • Has a builder mindset and can design scalable programs, not just one-off relationships

    Key criteria

    • Strategic business development — can identify and close partnerships that drive real commercial outcomes

    • Technical aptitude — enough depth to hold credible conversations with AI lab and product teams

    • Systems thinking — builds scalable programs, not just one-off deals

    • Access — personal relationships at the decision-maker level inside labs, AI-native companies, and the investor community

    Why this role is exciting

    • Ramp's AI partners are among the most influential partners any technology company can have right now. Getting this right matters enormously.

    • There is no playbook. Anyone who can do something distinctive here will create a significant advantage — for Ramp and for their own career.

    • This is one of the few roles that is genuinely AI-focused at a leading company in AI and technology.

    • Ramp is already embedded with leading AI companies and is ahead of the curve in building this function. The groundwork is there.

    • Ramp will give this person real runway — not a constrained, narrow mandate.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Every day will look different, but the work will include meeting with cross-functional stakeholders internally and externally, keeping a pulse on applied AI and the labs, negotiating active contracts, refining and executing Ramp's AI partnership strategy, and helping Ramp get closer to the teams that matter at the top AI companies.




NICE TO HAVES

 - The ideal candidate combines two qualities that are hard to find in one person:
   
   
   ECOSYSTEM CONNECTOR
   
   - Deep personal relationships in the San Francisco AI community — founders, lab leaders, and investors — at a level where people pick up the phone
   
   - Experience working inside or alongside leading AI partners in a way that provides genuine credibility, not just familiarity
   
   - Known and trusted by the venture capital and investor community in AI
   
   
   COMMERCIAL OPERATOR
   
   - Has built partnerships from zero at a high-growth company and been accountable for commercial outcomes
   
   - Can do the product and business development work simultaneously — technically fluent enough to engage on integrations and commercially sharp enough to close deals
   
   - Has a builder mindset and can design scalable programs, not just one-off relationships
   
   
   
   
   KEY CRITERIA
   
   - Strategic business development — can identify and close partnerships that drive real commercial outcomes
   
   - Technical aptitude — enough depth to hold credible conversations with AI lab and product teams
   
   - Systems thinking — builds scalable programs, not just one-off deals
   
   - Access — personal relationships at the decision-maker level inside labs, AI-native companies, and the investor community
   
   
   
   
   WHY THIS ROLE IS EXCITING
   
   - Ramp's AI partners are among the most influential partners any technology company can have right now. Getting this right matters enormously.
   
   - There is no playbook. Anyone who can do something distinctive here will create a significant advantage — for Ramp and for their own career.
   
   - This is one of the few roles that is genuinely AI-focused at a leading company in AI and technology.
   
   - Ramp is already embedded with leading AI companies and is ahead of the curve in building this function. The groundwork is there.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

You will be a front-line manager to a group of 6-8 CSMs, who each manage ~60 Activations at a given time in Ramp’s Mid Market portfolio. You will be responsible for developing and standardizing implementation best practices, 1:1 coaching and mentoring, building a repeatable and scalable customer activation motion that enables growth without proportional increases in team size, and working closely with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Operations, Risk, and Product to drive positive outcomes for this segment. As a key member of the Mid Market CSM leadership team, you will have the opportunity to help build and refine Ramp’s customer success and onboarding motion.

What You'll Do

  • Set and maintain a high-performing culture and morale by managing a group of exceptional CSMs to drive thorough and efficient onboarding and product activation for Ramp’s medium/large customers

  • Oversee the daily activities and quota performance management of individual CSMs to ensure team exceeds product onboarding and spend activation goals, while maintaining strong CSAT

  • Refine best practice playbooks for the CSM team, and improve team output and efficiency over time by optimizing systems and processes

  • Develop and execute career development and leadership plans for direct reports; inclusive of but not limited to daily 1:1 mentoring, coaching on sales skills, enhancing product knowledge, providing call feedback, and running enablement sessions

  • Act as a voice of the customer and key contributor retaining and expanding Ramp’s Mid Market segment

  • Build and leverage internal AI tools and Salesforce dashboards to monitor the success of our customers and the performance of the team

  • Report on team performance and forecast to senior leadership

  • Represent the CSM team cross-functionally with leaders of other departments

What You Need

  • 5+ years of implementation, CSM or AM experience as an individual contributor, with a proven, consistent track record exceeding goals

  • 3+ years of experience building and leading implementation or CSM teams with a proven track record of exceeding goals

  • Prior demonstrated success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS companies

  • Ability to identify trends, translate company strategy into team-level priorities, and drive initiatives that improve team metrics and organizational outcomes

  • Proven ability to coach teams on selling the full platform, not just individual products; experience driving multi-product adoption, cross-sell, and upsell across a book of business

  • Track record of pushing pace on input metrics, building repeatable playbooks, and optimizing systems and processes to improve team output

  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills across Sales, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams; demonstrated ability to represent Customer Success at a leadership level

  • Comfort with and curiosity about AI tools and their application to CS workflows; ability to lead a team through AI-driven process transformation and evaluate how AI can augment CSM productivity and customer outcomes

  • Strong understanding of customer financial workflows, including AP/AR, spend controls, and month-end close processes; ability to coach CSMs on ROI-grounded conversations with controllers and finance leaders

  • Proficiency in data analytics tools (Salesforce, Looker, and Excel) with the ability to leverage data to drive decisions, create systems, and identify process improvements.

Nice to Haves

  • CPA or equivalent accounting certification, or deep working knowledge of accounting software (e.g. NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, Sage)

  • Experience with financial services sales or selling into finance and accounting personas

  • Experience at a high-growth startup in an enterprise or mid-market customer success environment

  • Familiarity with contribution profit models or usage-based revenue metrics

  • Experience leading teams through AI adoption or workflow automation initiatives

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

Customers save an average of 16% on vendor spend annually and eliminate 46+ hours of manual purchasing work every month.

As a Procurement Product Activation Manager, you're the person who makes that real for our customers. You'll work directly with CFOs, controllers, and finance operations teams to design, configure, and launch Ramp's procurement product — helping them go from broken, manual buying processes to a streamlined system that their entire company actually uses.

This is not a "follow the playbook" implementation role. You'll be redesigning how companies buy things, which requires equal parts process consulting, product expertise, and relationship management.

🎯 What You'll Do

  • Own procurement implementation for Commercial and upper Mid-Market accounts from close-won through go-live

  • Partner with CFOs, finance ops, IT, and legal stakeholders to map existing procurement workflows and design their future-state on Ramp through a change management process

  • When procurement and Bill Pay are both part of the deal, cover both — procurement is the priority, but you carry Bill Pay activation when it's bundled

  • Provide structured product feedback to Ramp's Engineering and Product teams based on what you see across implementations — this is a core part of the role

  • Partner with AEs and AMs when procurement configuration questions come up pre-close or during expansion

🧠 What You Bring

  • Real procurement depth: you've lived inside procure-to-pay — whether at a company managing purchasing or at a platform like Coupa, Zip, Procurify, Stampli, or Ivalua. PO creation, approval routing, invoice matching, and ERP sync aren't concepts you read about; they're things you've configured or managed.

  • Customer-facing confidence: you run structured discovery, manage calls with multiple decision-makers, and can guide a Controller or AP Manager through a configuration decision without losing their trust

  • Strong follow-through: multiple implementations running at once, nothing falls through, customers don't have to chase you

  • Moves fast independently: Ramp's product ships constantly. You don't wait for someone to brief you on a new feature — you find it, figure it out, and update your approach.

  • Sharp product instincts: you can tell the difference between a user error, a training gap, and a real product limitation — and you say so directly to Engineering and Product, not just "the customer asked for X."

🌟 Nice to Have

  • Experience at a procurement software company in an implementation, solutions, or customer success role

  • Familiarity with NetSuite, QuickBooks, or other ERP systems and how they integrate with procurement tools

  • Consulting background or experience at a company where structured discovery was a core skill. You know how to lead a call and leave with clear requirements

🏆 What Success Looks Like

  • You're carrying 50–60 active implementations per quarter and customers are hitting go-live on schedule

  • Your CSM counterparts know what you're working on and why — handoffs are clean, nothing falls through the cracks between implementation and ongoing success

  • You've built or meaningfully improved at least one internal process — a playbook, a feedback loop with Product, a configuration template — that the team uses after you

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • One Medical annual membership

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

About the Role

We're looking for an experienced HRIS Analyst to join Ramp's People team during an active Workday implementation. Reporting to our Senior HRIS Manager, you'll play a hands-on role in configuration and system support, partnering closely with our implementation partner and cross-functional teams through go-live and hypercare.

This is an opportunity to help strengthen the data integrity, controls, and employee experience that support Ramp as we scale. You'll bring a solutions-focused, collaborative approach and strong systems thinking to a fast-moving, high-growth environment. The ideal candidate is naturally curious, understands how People data flows across systems, and looks for ways to streamline processes as they build them, staying flexible as priorities evolve along the way.

 

What You'll Do

  • Support the configuration, testing, rollout, and ongoing maintenance of Workday modules, including HCM, Benefits, Advanced Compensation, Time Tracking, and Absence

  • Partner with key stakeholders across the business to gather requirements, run testing cycles, resolve issues, and ensure cutover readiness

  • Run data validation and audits across HRIS and downstream systems, ensuring data integrity, security, and compliance through regular reporting

  • Support system releases and enhancements, including testing changes, documenting outcomes, and triaging issues as they arise

  • Train and enable team members and system users on existing and new processes and functionality

  • Build and maintain SOPs and job aids that make recurring HRIS processes accurate, scalable, and easy for others to support

  • Support AI transformation initiatives involving Workday, partnering with People, IT, Finance, and business stakeholders to evaluate and implement AI-driven solutions

     

What You Need

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on Workday experience, including configuration and production support

  • Direct experience with one or more Workday modules: HCM, Benefits, Advanced Compensation, Time Tracking, or Absence

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated ability to reconcile data, identify root causes, and troubleshoot discrepancies across systems.

  • Strong attention to detail and track record of managing employee data with sound judgment, accuracy, and appropriate controls

  • Ability to translate business requirements into configuration, testing, and documentation

  • Proactive problem-solver who takes initiative to resolve issues with minimal oversight

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to partner cross-functionally across People, Finance, IT and business stakeholders

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, evolving environment

 

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience supporting a Workday implementation post-production stabilization

  • Familiarity with Workday reporting, integrations, or security concepts

  • Exposure to automation tools or AI-assisted workflows

  • Background in a high-growth tech or fintech environment, ideally with global scope

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking an experienced Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) for its FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business entity. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and its Regulations, this role is the legally-appointed compliance officer responsible for implementing RBCC's AML/ATF compliance program and for reporting suspicious transactions to FINTRAC. This is a standalone, high-accountability compliance leadership role: you will own Ramp Canada’s AML program end to end, act as the primary point of contact for FINTRAC and Ramp’s financial partners in the region, and serve as the gatekeeper protecting Ramp's Canadian entity from financial crime.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as RBCC's MLRO, with authority over AML/ATF program design, execution, and effectiveness

  • Act as primary regulatory contact with FINTRAC, managing supervisory correspondence, reporting, and exam readiness

  • Make STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) filing determinations and file STRs

  • Run day-to-day transaction monitoring and sanctions screening triage and investigation for the Canadian book

  • -Own and maintain RBCC's AML/ATF risk assessment, refreshing it as products, geography, and risk profile evolve (including Quebec's onboarding)

  • Develop, document, and deliver RBCC's ongoing compliance training program

  • Define and stand up the operational workstreams for Canada, including case types, SLAs, escalation paths, tooling.

  • Negotiate and clarify AML/compliance requirements directly with BMO (our Canadian banking partner) and other partners as new products and use cases come online

  • Partner with Ramp's broader Compliance, Legal, and Regulatory Affairs teams (US) on cross-border projects and Canada's continued expansion

  • Partner with the Global team and the Engineering team to identify areas of opportunity for automation, and operational efficiency and lead AI-driven initiatives.

What You Need

  • 8+ years of financial services experience in compliance, AML, or related regulatory advisory roles, preferably in fintech or at an MSB

  • Deep working knowledge of FINTRAC's supervisory expectations and regulations

  • Direct experience interfacing with regulators and bank partners

  • AI Fluency and demonstrated experience leveraging AI to build and scale AML programs

  • Comfort operating as a standalone compliance lead with independent judgment on filing/escalation decisions

  • Experience building an AML program from a nascent/early stage, not only maintaining an established one

  • Fintech or payments domain experience (card issuing, corporate expense, high-velocity digital transaction monitoring) strongly preferred over traditional retail-branch compliance background

Nice-to-Haves

  • Fluency in French

  • Experience supporting an MSB registration/licensing process (e.g., provincial registrations such as Quebec)

  • Prior cross-border/group compliance structure experience

  • Data analysis skills

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

 

Ramp Applicant Privacy Notice

About the Role

Ramp's Strategic Finance team sits at the center of how the company allocates its time and resources. We're hiring across three complementary tracks — and looking for people with sharp financial instincts, a builder's mindset, and the drive to take on a large scope quickly. Whether you lean toward GTM strategy, FP&A infrastructure, or broad strategic partnership, this is a rare opportunity to shape a pre-IPO company at a pivotal moment in its growth.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own detailed financial and operational models with the highest quality and accuracy

  • Use data to influence key strategic decisions across Product, GTM, and business leadership

  • Lead planning analyses for cross-functional teams, evaluating tradeoffs across growth, efficiency, and resourcing

  • Identify and develop KPIs; build dashboards to monitor performance and communicate insights to stakeholders

  • Partner closely with business leaders to translate strategy into execution and drive accountability

  • Help run bi-annual budgeting and headcount planning cycles

  • Manage company performance against financial targets — identifying where to course-correct and where to accelerate

  • Build and maintain internal tools that reduce manual work and improve data accuracy across the finance org

 

What You Need

  • 4+ years in Investment Banking, Management Consulting, VC/PE, or Corporate Finance at a top-tier technology company

  • Excellent financial modeling and quantitative / data analysis skills

  • Extreme attention to detail with a high regard for precision

  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills

  • Track record of developing and maintaining relationships with internal and external partners

  • A "get things done" mentality — you dissect complex problems, find solutions, and drive them to completion with a high degree of autonomy

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and adapting to evolving priorities

 

Nice to Haves

  • Expertise with Looker, SQL, and/or Python

  • Systems thinking — you design processes to be reliable, scalable, and maintainable

  • Curiosity about AI tools — prior experience is a plus, but not required

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is launching payments across the EU through its Swedish payment institution. Our European operations team (Europs) onboards European businesses and keeps them trading, across Ramp's own regulated entities and our card-issuing and payments partners. We're a small team that runs on frontier AI tooling: our operators build and use their own automations so they can spend their time on judgement, not admin. We're hiring a KYB/AML Analyst in Stockholm to review and onboard business customers of our Swedish entity, work directly with those customers to get them live, and resolve onboarding requirements raised by our partners. You'll join a small Swedish team and help keep onboarding moving every day as we grow.

What You'll Do

  • Carry out first-line (1LoD) KYB reviews of business customers onboarding with Ramp's Swedish payment institution: company verification, beneficial ownership, sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening, and risk assessment

  • Decide standard cases end to end, and escalate complex or higher-risk cases with a clear rationale

  • Handle customer communications through onboarding: clear document requests, follow-ups and status updates

  • Resolve onboarding requirements from our card-issuing and payments partners for EU customers

  • Document decisions to a standard that holds up to second-line and regulatory review

  • Keep Swedish casework moving when teammates are on leave or handling incidents

  • Spend part of your time improving how we work: playbooks, templates and AI-assisted workflows

What You Need

  • 2–4 years of KYB / AML / onboarding experience at a fintech, payment institution, EMI or bank

  • Solid grounding in business customer due diligence: company registers, UBO identification, sanctions/PEP screening, and spotting red flags

  • Fluent English, written and verbal

  • Clear, friendly written communication with customers

  • Curiosity about AI tools and how they can make casework faster and better

  • Based in, or relocating to, Stockholm, with the right to work in Sweden

Nice-to-Haves

  • Swedish (strongly preferred)

  • Familiarity with Swedish sources and requirements (Bolagsverket, the beneficial ownership register, FI expectations under the Swedish AML Act)

  • Experience onboarding EU businesses across several jurisdictions

  • An additional European language

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About the Role

As one of the first Account Executives based in the UK, you’ll be focused on driving Ramp’s expansion in the European market. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp's first post-sales hire in Europe doesn't just activate customers, they set the standard for what post-sales excellence looks like in a brand new market. This is a role for people who have been inside organizations when change was hard, who speak the language of a CFO, and who can move a customer from onboarding to true business value without losing the commercial thread. You'll own a book of customers end-to-end: responsible for driving genuine activation and adoption, and for finding and closing the expansion opportunities that follow when customers are actually getting value. There is no handoff here. Onboarding and growth live in the same seat. As one of the first people on the ground in London, you'll have real accountability from day one, and the work you do will directly shape how Ramp builds its post-sales motion across Europe. If you're someone who uses AI the way high performers use any sharp tool (as a default, not an experiment), who is energized by building from scratch, and who wants to own outcomes rather than just execute a playbook, this is the role.

What You'll Do

  • Lead customers through the full transformation journey, from implementation through agentic workflow adoption.

  • Own the revenue target for your book of business.

  • Build and own the change management strategy for each account: map stakeholders, diagnose resistance, build internal coalitions, and drive adoption past the finish line.

  • Quantify and communicate Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about

  • Help customers understand and adopt Ramp's agentic finance capabilities, positioning new workflows not as features, but as fundamental changes to how their finance team operates.

  • Maintain tight feedback loops with Design & Engineering, ensuring market signals from customers land where they can drive product decisions.

  • Support the GM on the highest-priority strategic initiatives of the moment; competitive landscape, ICP refinement, new segment exploration, and more.

What You Need

  • Right to work in the UK is required. Willingness to travel frequently across the UK and Europe.

  • Founder-mode mentality with proof to back it up. You own outcomes, not deliverables and you have a track record of building, selling, or figuring something out on your own. You make fast decisions with incomplete data and don't wait for a playbook that doesn't exist yet.

  • AI fluency as a daily habit. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment.

  • Deep product expertise that translates into prescriptive recommendations. You know Ramp's full range of products, integrations, and configuration options inside out and you use that knowledge to anticipate customer needs and position solutions before they ask.

  • Technical acumen to hold your own with Product and Engineering on integrations, APIs, and workflow architecture.

  • Commercial instinct. You proactively identify expansion opportunities and know how to turn customer success into revenue growth.

  • Strong written and verbal communication.

  • High frustration tolerance and resilience. Building from scratch means things will break constantly.

Nice to Haves

  • Fluency in additional European languages

  • Experience in a high-growth startup, consulting, VC, IB/PE, or other analytically intensive environments

  • Exposure to fintech, SaaS, or B2B sales cycles

  • Track record of entrepreneurial activity: founding a company, running a meaningful side project, or building something from zero

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • One Medical annual membership

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Comfort working across the stack, including API design and backend systems, even with frontend as your center of gravity

  • A track record of shipping polished, production-grade product experiences and owning them through ambiguity

  • Bonus: experience with BI tools, data visualization, or financial/analytics products

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp's Brand team ships a high volume of ambitious creative across product launches, growth, events, customer marketing, and brand awareness. As the work has scaled, so has the need for a strong operating system around it.

We're hiring a Director of Brand Operations to build that operating system: the processes, milestones, and cross-functional coordination that let a world-class creative team do its best work and ship fast. This is an operations role focused on how the work gets done; it is not a traditional production-management role.

You'll be the operator who protects creatives from organizational swirl, sets clear ways of working, and fixes cross-functional breakdowns upstream so great ideas reach the world quickly.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and build the operating system for how Brand's creative gets produced.

  • Build the brand operating system: the processes, milestones, and ways of working that turn creative direction into shipped work.

  • Diagnose and fix bottlenecks across functions. Find where work stalls, trace it to the source, and remove the limiting factor wherever it lives.

  • Protect creatives from org swirl by absorbing cross-functional complexity so the team stays focused on the work.

  • Automate with AI: use AI to streamline how work flows and cut manual overhead across the operation (intake, triage, status, reporting, handoffs).

  • Partner with the creative leads so operations and creative are complementary, freeing creative leads to focus on creative.

  • Be Brand's ambassador to the rest of Ramp: scope incoming work and pull Brand into projects early, at the right time.

What You Need

  • Exceptional organization: you hold 20+ live workstreams and keep everyone on track

  • A cross-functional root-cause instinct: you can walk into a tangled, multi-team workflow, explain why it's slow, and fix it. This is the most important capability for the role.

  • A track record of building systems and automation: you've taken an operation from messy to repeatable and use tooling and AI to compress cycle time.

  • A metrics-driven approach: you instrument delivery so progress is clear and provable.

  • Hands-on, lean leadership: you lift both the operation and the people in it.

  • A bias for better ways of working: you remove limiting factors and speed up delivery without adding process for its own sake.

  • An operator-first profile: we care more about someone who can diagnose and fix how work flows than about a creative, production, or marketing pedigree. Strong candidates come from product ops, biz ops, GTM ops, finance ops, or chief-of-staff backgrounds.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience scaling an in-house creative or content studio in a high-growth environment.

  • Experience building AI-assisted operational workflows.

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp's Advisory & Services channel is one of the most strategically important growth levers in the business. As an Advisory& Services Partner Development Representative (PDR), you'll be the engine behind acquiring, reactivating, and qualifying the consulting firms, System Integrators (SIs), and advisory practices that refer, implement, or integrate Ramp for their clients.

You'll be holding conversations with partnership heads, business development leads,Managing Directors, and practice leads at consulting firms, ERP implementation shops, and strategic advisory practices - building relationships that turn into signed referral agreements and a pipeline of activated partners that are Ramp champions.

This role is perfect for someone who:

  • Is gritty and relentless - comfortable reaching out to firm leaders who are slow to respond and keeps going anyway

  • Carries real executive presence and can credibly hold a conversation with a Partner or MD at a top-tier firm

  • Has a strong client hand - naturally curious about how consulting and advisory firms serve their clients, and speaks their language

  • Thrives when the playbook is still being written and takes ownership of building it

  • Embraces AI to augment and automate processes to drive greater efficiencies for workflows

What You'll Do

  • Source and qualify net new consulting, advisory, and technology partners that can drive referral pipeline and commercial value to Ramp, focused on firms with active CFO-level client relationships

  • Build top-of-funnel pipeline for Channel Partner Managers by qualifying partner candidates against Ramp's tiering criteria and handing off warm, ready-to-activate relationships

  • Reactivate dormant services partners across Ramp's existing book of ~400 consulting, technology, and advisory firms - identifying which relationships have gone cold and reigniting them through strategic, senior-level outreach

  • Identify and engage system integrators (SIs) and ERP implementation specialists - specifically firms in the NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Dynamics, and Odoo ecosystems - to build Ramp's productized SI implementation program

  • Craft outbound messaging and campaigns tailored to services partner archetypes - boutique firms, PE-focused advisory practices, tech consulting firms, and ERP implementation shops

  • Maintain accurate partner and opportunity data in Salesforce; track pipeline health across both dormant reactivation and net new acquisition motions

  • Leverage AI tools and lightweight automations to scale partner outreach, surface reactivation opportunities, and build repeatable workflows across a high-volume partner book

What You Need

  • Grit and drive to run a high-volume, high-quality outbound motion against senior contacts who are hard to reach - and the persistence to keep going

  • Executive presence: you can hold a credible conversation with a Partner or Managing Director at a consulting or advisory firm, and they take you seriously

  • Deep understanding of how consulting firms go to market, how they serve CXO-level clients, and drive influence

  • A client-oriented mindset - you lead with what's in it for the partner's business, not just Ramp's

  • Strong written communication skills - outreach that is pithy, credible, and gets responses from senior people at busy firms

  • Comfort managing a large, segmented partner book and staying disciplined across long reactivation and qualification cycles

  • 1-3 years of experience in partnerships, channel sales, business development, or sales development or as a business analyst in a strategy consulting firm (e.g., McKinsey, Bain, BCG)

  • Bachelor's degree from a four-year university


Nice to Haves

  • Background at - or selling to - consulting firms, strategy practices, Systems Integrators (SIs) or advisory businesses

  • Exposure to ERP ecosystems: NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Odoo, or similar implementation partner communities

  • Familiarity with how system integrators operate: how they price services, staff implementations, and build revenue relationships with technology vendors

  • Experience working in a partner channel that was still being built - first rep in a motion or early team member in a new GTM track

  • Background in B2B fintech, SaaS, or financial services

  • Familiarity with Salesforce or similar CRM tools

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (specifically Claude Code), building basic automations (bots, workflows, etc.) to drive efficiency in a sales, partnerships, or business development context

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay
