The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

You'll join Ramp's travel team, which builds two products, Ramp Travel and Juno. Both integrate with a growing network of travel management company (TMC) partners. You'll be our expert on how those integrations work in practice: how content (search, booking and changes), payments, approvals, servicing and reporting flow between our products and each TMC.

You'll own the operational side of each partnership, from the day it's signed through every customer that goes live on it. You'll work closely with engineering, our customer success managers, and the teams that sign new TMC partners and bring in customers through them, but you won't own those commercial relationships.

Success means each new TMC goes live more efficiently than the last, mutual customers on each TMC go live faster and more smoothly over time as your playbooks improve, and the TMC servicing experience for Ramp and Juno travelers is seamless and delightful.

The travel team is small and building quickly across both products, so everyone works beyond the edges of their role. Alongside your core work, you'll help wherever the team needs it most.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and refine our playbook for standing up a new TMC partner, and work with engineering to take each new TMC from signed partnership to its first live mutual customer.

  • For each live TMC, build the playbook for adding mutual customers and new points of sale, including in new countries and regions. Support CSMs when a rollout needs TMC-specific setup.

  • Investigate with engineering when bookings, payments or data don't flow correctly, and see fixes through with the TMC.

  • Train TMC agents who service accounts through our dashboards. For TMCs that use their own tools, make sure our workflows fit theirs.

  • Create SOPs for TMC agents to ensure they deliver top tier support for travelers.

  • Keep TMC partners up to date on product changes that affect them, and answer their agents' questions.

  • Always get to the why behind a TMC ask and make sure that it’s the best path forward. Just because something is done a certain way doesn’t mean that it’s the right or only way.

  • Actively track and analyze data to manage and measure the quality of the travel support experience offered by our partners.

  • Join partner review calls to represent day-to-day operations.

  • Identify the steps in your playbooks that can be automated or built into the product, and work with product and engineering to make that happen.

  • Take on work beyond your core role, such as joining Juno's customer support rotation, where you'll see firsthand how our partner integrations shape the customer experience.

What You Need

  • 5+ years in implementation, partner operations, technical consulting, or a similar partner- or customer-facing technical role, ideally in travel technology, SaaS or fintech.

  • Corporate travel domain experience, such as working at a TMC or with GDSs (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport), NDC content, or travel mid- and back-office systems.

  • Technical fluency to troubleshoot integrations and data flows across systems and hold credible conversations with engineers. Engineering depth is not required.

  • Experience managing external partners or vendors, and working cross-functionally with customer success, product and engineering.

  • Strong written communication, including the ability to train others and explain technical issues to nontechnical audiences.

  • AI fluency as a daily habit. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment.

  • Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments, with a bias toward action and a high level of ownership.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Technical fluency with APIs, integrations, debugging, or data analysis, even if you do not write production code.

  • Experience in B2B SaaS, travel, fintech, or another operationally complex product.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role


As an AI Solutions Strategist, you will sit at the intersection of customers, AI delivery, and Ramp’s core product teams. You will partner with enterprise/strategic customers to deeply understand their finance workflows—especially corporate finance and controllership priorities like close, controls, and spend governance—identify high-impact opportunities for AI and automation, and translate those needs into clear problem statements, solution designs, and actionable feedback for Ramp’s Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams.

This role is for someone who can listen carefully, structure ambiguity, and turn on-the-ground learnings into scalable solutions. This role required high proactivity and bias to action.

 

What You'll Do

  • Discover and diagnose customer needs. Run stakeholder interviews and workflow deep dives with Finance, Procurement, AP, and IT teams. Map end-to-end processes and identify the underlying drivers behind pain points — risk, cost, cycle time, compliance, exception volume, and operational complexity.

  • Translate needs into solution requirements. Turn qualitative input into crisp artifacts: problem statements, success metrics, constraints, acceptance criteria, and deployment plans. Balance speed, safety, and scalability across MVPs, iterations, and broader rollouts.

  • Partner with technical teams to implement AI workflows. Work closely with Ramp engineers and AI builders to design and ship solutions that meet real customer workflows. Specify data inputs, integrations, governance needs, policy rules, auditability requirements, and edge cases.

  • Drive feedback loops into Ramp's product. Synthesize learnings across customers into reusable patterns and product opportunities. Write high-signal briefs for Product and Engineering that explain what customers need, why it matters, and what should be built next.

  • Communicate impact and guide executives. Present status, outcomes, and recommendations to customer operators, executives, and internal stakeholders. Quantify impact through time saved, error reduction, improved compliance, faster close, and other business outcomes.

 

What You Need

  • 4+ years of relevant experience

  • Strong customer empathy and the ability to earn trust quickly with senior stakeholders.

  • Excellent problem framing: you can turn messy workflows into clear systems and priorities.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and iterating quickly while keeping quality high.

  • Ability to communicate clearly in writing (briefs, requirements, postmortems) and verbally (workshops, exec readouts).

  • A builder mindset: you like shipping, learning, and improving the system.

  • Experience in solutions, implementation, product strategy, consulting, or technical program management.

  • Strong grounding in corporate finance / controllership workflows, including accounting close, spend governance/controls, budgeting, procurement, and AP operations.

  • Experience translating finance requirements into system design and configuration (e.g., ERP/accounting, procurement, expense management, payments), including integrations, data mapping, and controls.

  • Ability to partner with finance system owners/admins to drive change management, testing (UAT), and successful rollouts.

  • Familiarity with finance operations workflows (AP, procurement, expenses, cards, accounting close).

  • Exposure to AI-enabled products, automation, or applied ML (you do not need to be an ML engineer).

  • Basic comfort with data concepts and systems integration (APIs, ETL, SQL, spreadsheets, data quality).

 

Working style

We collaborate best when we’re close to the work and close to each other. This role is hybrid in New York, with time in-office to partner tightly with product and engineering teams. Importantly, this role required spending time with customers to understand real workflows, so travel and flexibility are critical to success.

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

ABOUT THE ROLE 


As an AI Solutions Strategist, you will sit at the intersection of customers, AI delivery, and Ramp’s core product teams. You will partner with enterprise/strategic customers to deeply understand their finance workflows—especially corporate finance and controllership priorities like close, controls, and spend governance—identify high-impact opportunities for AI and automation, and translate those needs into clear problem statements, solution designs, and actionable feedback for Ramp’s Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams.

This role is for someone who can listen carefully, structure ambiguity, and turn on-the-ground learnings into scalable solutions. This role required high proactivity and bias to action.

 




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Discover and diagnose customer needs. Run stakeholder interviews and workflow deep dives with Finance, Procurement, AP, and IT teams. Map end-to-end processes and identify the underlying drivers behind pain points — risk, cost, cycle time, compliance, exception volume, and operational complexity.

 - Translate needs into solution requirements. Turn qualitative input into crisp artifacts: problem statements, success metrics, constraints, acceptance criteria, and deployment plans. Balance speed, safety, and scalability across MVPs, iterations, and broader rollouts.

 - Partner with technical teams to implement AI workflows. Work closely with Ramp engineers and AI builders to design and ship solutions that meet real customer workflows. Specify data inputs, integrations, governance needs, policy rules, auditability requirements, and edge cases.

 - Drive feedback loops into Ramp's product. Synthesize learnings across customers into reusable patterns and product opportunities. Write high-signal briefs for Product and Engineering that explain what customers need, why it matters, and what should be built next.

 - Communicate impact and guide executives. Present status, outcomes, and recommendations to customer operators, executives, and internal stakeholders. Quantify impact through time saved, error reduction, improved compliance, faster close, and other business outcomes.



 


WHAT YOU NEED

 - 4+ years of relevant experience

 - Strong customer empathy and the ability to earn trust quickly with senior stakeholders.

 - Excellent problem framing: you can turn messy workflows into clear systems and priorities.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity and iterating quickly while keeping quality high.

 - Ability to communicate clearly in writing (briefs, requirements, postmortems) and verbally (workshops, exec readouts).

 - A builder mindset: you like shipping, learning, and improving the system.

 - Experience in solutions, implementation, product strategy, consulting, or technical program management.

 - Strong grounding in corporate finance / controllership workflows, including accounting close, spend governance/controls, budgeting, procurement, and AP operations.

 - Experience translating finance requirements into system design and configuration (e.g., ERP/accounting, procurement, expense management, payments), including integrations, data mapping, and controls.

 - Ability to partner with finance system owners/admins to drive change management, testing (UAT), and successful rollouts.

 - Familiarity with finance operations workflows (AP, procurement, expenses, cards, accounting close).

 - Exposure to AI-enabled products, automation, or applied ML (you do not need to be an ML engineer).

 - Basic comfort with data concepts and systems integration (APIs, ETL, SQL, spreadsheets, data quality).

We collaborate best when we’re close to the work and close to each other. This role is hybrid in New York, with time in-office to partner tightly with product and engineering teams. About Ramp

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Business Systems Engineer to own and evolve Ramp’s Quote-to-Cash systems. You’ll build and maintain Ramp’s Salesforce-based quoting platform, contract workflows, and Billing/Core integrations that turn complex commercial agreements into accurate, supportable customer outcomes—from quote creation and approvals through order forms, provisioning, billing, renewals, and amendments.

This is not a Salesforce CPQ implementation role. Ramp uses an in-house Quote-to-Cash platform built on Salesforce, so we’re looking for a strong Salesforce engineer with experience in quoting, pricing, contracts, billing, subscriptions, or other complex commercial workflows.

This role sits in Growth Engineering’s Business Systems Engineering team and partners closely with Deal Desk, Legal, Finance, Billing Engineering, Product, and GTM teams. You’ll combine hands-on Salesforce engineering with systems design and strong commercial judgment to make high-stakes revenue workflows reliable, scalable, and easier for teams to use.

 
 

What You’ll Do

  • Design, develop, test, and deploy applications on the Salesforce Platform.

  • Design, build, and operate Ramp’s Salesforce-based Quote-to-Cash platform and the integrations between Salesforce, Ironclad, Billing/Core, and adjacent business systems. Own data contracts, idempotency, error handling, reconciliation, and safe lifecycle changes for quotes, contracts, and subscriptions.

  • Design, develop, and maintain integration solutions using in-house services and approved automation platforms.

  • Drive architecture, tooling, and design decisions that keep commercial systems fast, reliable, and scalable.

  • Write and communicate technical specifications, including architecture diagrams, data models, process flows, and sequence diagrams.

  • Own data integrity and the operating assumptions for your domain; continually improve them.

  • Partner with the rest of the team on code reviews, operational support, debugging, and solution design.

What You’ll Need

  • 7+ years building applications on the Salesforce Platform.

  • 5+ years of systems architecture and integration experience.

  • Strong hands-on experience with Apex, triggers, Lightning Web Components, Flows, and asynchronous processing.

  • Working knowledge of another programming language, such as Python.

  • Strong API and integration-design skills, including reliable handling of retries, duplicate events, partial failures, and data reconciliation.

  • Experience with Quote-to-Cash domains such as quoting, pricing, approvals, contract lifecycle management, billing, subscriptions, renewals, or amendments. Experience with Salesforce CPQ is welcome but not required.

  • Familiarity with the broader GTM stack beyond Salesforce, such as Gong, LeanData, contract lifecycle management, billing, or revenue systems.

  • Strong knowledge of synchronous and asynchronous integration patterns, streaming APIs, and publish/subscribe architectures.

  • Working knowledge of data pipelines, CI/CD, Salesforce platform limits, code coverage, and unit-testing practices.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex commercial requirements into simple, durable system behavior with non-engineering partners.

  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully and evaluating their output.

Nice to Haves

  • Snowflake/DBT

  • Kafka experience

  • Experience with Agile methodologies

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

You will serve as a front-line manager for a team of Sales Development Representatives, responsible for outbound prospecting and pipeline generation across Ramp’s SMB segment.

You will lead and evolve the SMB sales development motion by providing 1:1 coaching, onboarding, training, and mentorship; setting team strategy; and partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Executive Leadership to drive pipeline and business outcomes.

As a member of the Sales Leadership team, you will play a critical role in developing SDR talent, scaling effective outbound practices, and continuously refining Ramp’s SMB go-to-market motion.

What You'll Do

  • Build and scale the SMB SDR function by evolving team operating rhythms, playbooks, coaching standards, and processes for an open-territory outbound motion.

  • Set and maintain a high-performing culture by overseeing daily SDR activity, pipeline generation, and quota performance to ensure key performance metrics are met.

  • Hire, onboard, and train new SDRs on Ramp’s products, buyer personas, competitive landscape, prospecting strategy, and tools through hands-on methods including role-plays.

  • Develop and execute career-growth and leadership plans for direct reports, including daily 1:1 mentorship and coaching on time management, objection handling, prospecting tactics, active listening, and pipeline creation.

  • Coach SDRs on effective multichannel outbound prospecting, including account research, relevant messaging, call execution, and using AI tools to improve efficiency and quality.

  • Partner with AEs and Sales and Marketing counterparts on pipeline-generation, territory, and prospecting initiatives that support SMB business objectives.

  • Report on team performance, pipeline health, and forecasts to senior leadership.

  • Improve team output and efficiency over time by identifying opportunities to optimize systems, processes, enablement, and AI-supported workflows.

  • Establish and maintain a library of prospecting resources, best practices, and training materials for the SMB SDR team.

  • Represent the SMB Sales Development team cross-functionally with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Product, and other departments.

What You Need

  • Minimum of 2 years of quota-carrying sales experience as an individual contributor, with a proven, consistent track record exceeding goals

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience building and leading sales development teams with a proven track record of exceeding goal

  • Prior demonstrated success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS companies, and history of consistently performing above quota in an outbound sales environment

  • A passion and excitement for hiring, with a thoughtful approach to team planning and development

  • Ability to articulate contractual, technical, and financial value points to customers, including executive leaders

  • Proficiency in data analytics tools (ie. Salesforce, Looker, and Excel) and familiarity with email and call automation platforms

  • High proficiency with AI tools (Claude, OpenAI, etc.), with the ability to incorporate tooling into prospecting, coaching, team workflows, and process improvement to drive greater SDR productivity

  • Ability to leverage data to drive decisions, create systems, and identify process improvements to improve efficiency

  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills, demonstrated through excellent communication and presentation skills

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with financial services sales in a full cycle sales role

  • Experience at a high-growth startup

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

 

Ramp Applicant Privacy Notice

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the role

Ramp is building its UK partnerships ecosystem, and we're looking for a Channel Partner Manager who can turn relationships across a myriad of industries into meaningful customer opportunities. This is a generalist role for someone who can see where a partnership makes sense, move quickly, and build momentum across a varied partner portfolio.

You'll identify how and where Ramp can create value for a prospective partner's customer base, then carry the relationship through to qualified introductions and customer adoption. You'll learn what uniquely motivates each partner and turn early success into a repeatable flywheel of referrals. Some relationships will need to be built from the ground up; others will need sharper activation and follow-through. The mix will evolve, so you should be comfortable moving between different partner models while staying focused on commercial outcomes.

You'll work closely with Ramp's UK Sales team and colleagues in Partnerships, Marketing, Events, Product, and Engineering to connect the right partners and customers and make each introduction count.

What you'll do

  • Build and manage a varied portfolio of UK partners, adapting your approach to each relationship and industry.

  • Identify how Ramp can create value for a prospective partner's customer base, then prioritize relationships with the clearest path to fast execution.

  • Understand what matters to each partner and shape a referral motion that gives them a compelling reason to keep bringing relevant customers to Ramp.

  • Create repeatable sources of qualified introductions through partner enablement, account mapping, joint campaigns, events, and warm networks.

  • Use business communities, hospitality, and executive events when they can create relevant introductions and measurable commercial value.

  • Coordinate partner introductions and follow-up with Ramp's Sales team so opportunities have a clear owner and a strong customer experience.

  • Track partner activity from introduction through qualified opportunity and customer adoption; use the data to refine each motion and focus time on what works.

  • Run regular partner reviews, keep commitments moving across teams, and represent Ramp credibly with partner executives and prospective customers.

What you need

  • 5+ years of experience, including 3+ years in partnerships, business development, partner sales, account management, or commercial strategy.

  • A record of building trusted senior relationships and delivering measurable commercial results through partners.

  • The ability to learn different partner business models quickly, understand their customers, and spot where Ramp can create value.

  • Strong commercial judgement in prioritizing prospects, shaping warm introductions, and managing opportunities with sales teams.

  • Experience executing partner go-to-market activity, such as enablement, account mapping, campaigns, events, or co-sell programs.

  • Comfort using performance data to assess partner activity, report results, and adjust course.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and listening skills, with the ability to work across partner organizations and internal teams.

  • A hands-on, organized working style that keeps multiple relationships and commitments moving at once.

  • UK-based, with flexibility to travel across the UK and attend occasional evening or weekend partner events.

Nice to haves

  • A background in strategy consulting or investment banking.

  • Experience creating B2B pipeline through partner networks, executive events, hospitality, or account-based campaigns.

  • Familiarity with UK small and medium-sized businesses and the finance leaders who buy and use Ramp's products.

  • Experience building a new partner motion in a growing market or adapting a successful approach to a new partner category.

What success looks like

  • Ramp has a prioritized UK partner portfolio with a clear customer opportunity and path to activation for each active relationship.

  • Partners and Ramp teams know who owns each introduction, opportunity, and next step.

  • Partner activity produces a consistent flow of relevant introductions, qualified opportunities, and customers.

  • Partners continue to bring relevant referrals because the relationship creates value for their customers and for their own business.

  • The strongest partner motions are repeatable, and the team has evidence to decide where to invest next.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

 

Ramp Applicant Privacy Notice

About the Role

Ramp is seeking a Fraud Operations Manager to help build and lead a team of Fraud Operations Specialists responsible for the efficient and effective execution of fraud detection and prevention strategies across all of Ramp’s products, enabling Ramp’s rapid growth. This role requires the ability to balance people management, process engineering, strategic thinking, and planning. You will utilize data and analytics to lead an efficient team, identify opportunities for improvement, prioritize development, and collaborate with cross-functional teams to operationalize policies, develop tools, and infrastructure that best support Ramp’s operations.

What You'll Do

  • Manage and continue building a team of Fraud Operations Specialists who manage & review alerts, conduct investigations, and recover funds through enabling right sized coverage and meeting service level agreements (SLA)

  • Develop a deep understanding of Ramp’s risk management policies (underwriting, payments, transactions, credit limit changes, collections) across all products

  • Partner with Product, Engineering and Data Science teams to build best in class risk tooling to increase operational efficiency

  • Partner with risk strategy teams to create a closed loop process to enhance policies and procedures

  • Leverage data and analytics to evaluate and prioritize solutions to improve operational efficiency

  • Research emerging fraud trends to innovate on Ramp's decisioning systems and policies

  • Help coordinate and respond to incidents through on-call duties as needed – in addition to customer escalations or sensitive case handling

  • Partner with Customer Support to educate and create awareness on fraud prevention best practices, identifying social engineering attempts, and support customers

What You Need

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in risk management including account takeovers and a broad range of payment related fraud

  • Minimum 2 years of experience building and managing teams

  • Strong background in process development and improvement

  • Investigative and critical thinking skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Experience integrating AI into your daily work

  • Experience within consumer/corporate/small business cards, payments, invoices, lending, or related industries

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with Regulation E, NACHA & Visa Core rules and regulations

  • Experience with Zendesk and Retool

  • Experience in high growth startups

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

Ramp is in a critical phase of growth, and marketing is one of the biggest drivers of it. We're building out our business systems team to make sure the systems behind every campaign, list, and lead can keep up.   • Own top-of-funnel marketing systems: the roadmap, the architecture decisions inside them, and their operational health

  • Run HubSpot as a system, not just a tool: workflows, lists, forms, properties, lifecycle stages, and the permissions and naming conventions that keep it from sprawling

The Applied Science team builds models and tools that solve Ramp’s most critical problems: from underwriting businesses to combatting fraud to making spend management smarter. We’re deeply embedded in the business and provide a quantitative foundation for decision making.

As an Applied Science intern, you’ll be a fully integrated member of the team and own your project from start to finish. Working with engineers, product managers, and business stakeholders, you’ll translate complex business needs into scalable machine-learning-driven solutions. This is a chance to apply ML concretely, ship code, and create genuine value for Ramp and our customers.

You will focus on exciting problems in areas like: credit, fraud, growth, or our core product.

 

What You’ll Do

  • End-to-End ML: own the model lifecycle from data exploration and feature engineering to training, benchmarking, deployment, and monitoring

  • State-of-the-Art AI: leverage the latest Large Language Models (LLMs) to solve novel problems and create new product capabilities for our customers

  • Versatile Techniques: apply the right tools to the right problems, whether it’s deep learning, gradient boosting, or causal inference

  • Rigorous Experimentation: quantify the impact of your work through A/B tests and other statistical methods

  • Collaborate: partner closely with product and business leaders to translate models and insights into actionable strategy and user-facing features

 

What You Need

  • B.S., M.S. or Ph.D. Student: currently pursuing a degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Math, Physics, Economics, Statistics, or other quantitative fields with an expected graduation date between Dec 2027 - 2029. Graduate degrees are preferred, but not a must.

  • Strong ML Fundamentals: solid understanding of the mathematical foundations of machine learning, statistics, probability, and optimization

  • Strong Interest or Experience with AI: curiosity and drive to integrate cutting edge LLMs and agents into applied solutions

  • Python Proficiency: good grasp of common Data Science libraries (pandas, scikit-learn, NumPy, PyTorch, etc.)

  • SQL Knowledge: experience wrangling data in a modern data warehouse (e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Clickhouse)

  • Practical Experience: track record of curating datasets and building/evaluating ML models

  • Strong Communication: ability to clearly explain complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences and use data to build a compelling narrative

  • Bias For Action: a comfort with ambiguity and desire to ship solutions quickly then iterate

 

Nice to Haves

  • Publications, Projects, or Previous Experience: relevant experience applying AI/ML and demonstrating your passion for the field

  • Production ML Mindset: knowledge of software engineering best practices applied to ML including version control (Git), testing, and writing maintainable code

  • Data Orchestration: experience with leveraging modern data orchestration platforms (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect, Metaflow)

 

Compensation

  • The monthly rate for this internship is $12,500 USD + housing stipend

  • Weekly coffee stipend

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the role

Ramp is building the future of work with AI. We’re bringing a new class of AI-native products to market that can understand business context, make decisions, and increasingly execute work on behalf of customers.

We’re looking for an AI Account Executive to help build the commercial motion for this emerging portfolio. You’ll own the full sales cycle, from creating pipeline and shaping the customer’s problem through evaluation, close, and activation. You’ll work across Engineering, IT, Security, and Procurement to turn complex AI capabilities into clear business outcomes.

This is a founding seller role. You’ll help define the market, qualification criteria, sales process, messaging, and playbooks that the broader organization will use. The right person is both a closer and a builder: someone who can win important early customers, learn quickly from the field, and turn those lessons into a repeatable system. We’re hiring AI Account Executives at multiple levels. The scope of the role, title, and compensation will reflect your experience and demonstrated ability to lead complex sales cycles and build new commercial motions.

What you’ll do

  • Own the full sales cycle: Source, qualify, develop, and close net-new opportunities for Ramp’s AI products, with accountability for pipeline creation, revenue, and forecast accuracy.

  • Create demand in an emerging category: Help customers identify high-value AI use cases, connect technical capabilities to urgent business problems, and build conviction before a mature buying process exists.

  • Navigate complex buying groups. Multi-thread across Finance, Engineering, IT, Security, Procurement, and executive stakeholders to align technical requirements, economic value, and organizational priorities.

  • Build the business case: Quantify ROI, total cost of ownership, operational impact, and risk reduction to earn executive sponsorship and create urgency.

  • Lead rigorous evaluations: Partner with Solutions, Product, and Engineering to scope demonstrations, pilots, security reviews, and implementation plans that establish a credible path to production.

  • Shape the commercial narrative: Pressure-test positioning, discovery, pricing, objection handling, and competitive messaging through direct customer engagement.

  • Turn field learning into a playbook: Document repeatable qualification criteria, buyer patterns, use cases, proof points, and deal strategies that improve the performance of future sellers.

  • Influence the product roadmap: Build a tight feedback loop with Product and Engineering by clearly communicating what customers value, where deals stall, and which capabilities will unlock adoption.

  • Operate as a founding team member: Help establish the standards, culture, tooling, and operating cadence for Ramp’s AI sales organization.

What you need

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets in complex B2B software sales, whether you’re an experienced AE ready for a new challenge or a seasoned enterprise seller looking to build something new.

  • Experience owning multi-stakeholder sales cycles from pipeline generation through close, ideally involving six-figure contracts or enterprise customers.

  • Demonstrated success selling a new product, emerging category, or technical solution without relying on a fully established playbook.

  • Strong discovery and business-case development skills, including the ability to quantify ROI, total cost of ownership, and measurable operational outcomes.

  • Technical fluency and intellectual curiosity: you can credibly discuss integrations, data flows, security, reliability, and AI capabilities with technical stakeholders without resorting to hand-waving.

  • Executive presence and the ability to communicate clearly with CFOs, CTOs, Finance leaders, Engineering teams, Procurement, and Security.

  • Strong pipeline discipline, forecasting judgment, and familiarity with structured sales methodologies such as MEDDICC, Command of the Message, or similar frameworks.

  • High agency and comfort operating in ambiguity. When the answer or playbook doesn’t exist, your instinct is to build it.

Ramp is seeking an experienced Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) for Ramp Advisory LLC, our SEC-registered investment adviser. This is a high-accountability, build-and-own role. You will own and be accountable for the firm's compliance program in house, and be the gatekeeper who protects clients and the firm while keeping pace with how fast Ramp ships product. You will report to Ramp's Head of Compliance, with direct access to Ramp Advisory's senior leadership.

 

What You'll Do

  • Serve as Ramp Advisory LLC’s designated CCO, with independent authority over the design, execution and effectiveness of the compliance program

  • Oversee key financial partners and vendors from a compliance standpoint

  • Shape customer onboarding strategy, partnering with Product, Engineering and Customer Experience to build scalable controls and monitoring

  • Experience in the fintech space

  • Deep working knowledge of the Advisers Act and SEC expectations

  • Direct experience supporting SEC examinations and interfacing with regulators

  • Experience overseeing custodian, broker-dealer or sub-adviser relationships

  • Sound, independent judgment: the ability to make and defend compliance decisions in real time, grounded in regulatory guidance, and to hold a position with senior stakeholders

  • Comfort operating as a standalone compliance lead in a fast-moving environment

  • Experience building controls and leading program design initiatives in partnership with engineering teams and cross-functional partners

About the Role

We're looking for an Employment Counsel to join Ramp's Legal team. This is a generalist employment role with broad scope. You will handle U.S. employment counseling as your base load, cover non-U.S. jurisdictions as needed, and own immigration and global mobility. You will partner directly with People, Talent, Total Rewards, Finance, Tax, Equity Admin, Compliance, and business leaders, and you will manage outside counsel in jurisdictions where we do not hold the expertise in house. We are a small, high-leverage team supporting a company that moves quickly, so you will cover a lot of ground and be trusted to run matters independently.

What You'll Do

  • Day-to-day employment counseling: Advise People partners and managers on hiring, worker classification, compensation, leaves and accommodations, performance management, discipline, separations, and more

  • Immigration and global mobility: Collaborate with the People team on the immigration program, including work authorization outside the U.S. Set and communicate the sponsorship policy, manage outside immigration counsel and case volume, and partner with Talent on offer-stage decisions. Support relocations, cross-border remote work requests, and business travel, and work with Finance and Tax on permanent establishment and mobility tax exposure

  • Investigations: Collaborate with the People team on internal investigations and advise on findings and outcomes

  • Disputes: Handle demand letters, agency charges, arbitrations, and litigation with outside counsel

  • Agreements and templates: Own offer letters, employment agreements, separation and release agreements, contractor and consultant agreements, restrictive covenants, and the local-law variants of each

  • Transactions: Support employment and immigration diligence, employee transitions, and post-close integration for M&A and new-market entry

  • Build for scale: Produce manager training, policies, self-serve guidance, and repeatable processes as we expand in the US and globally

What You Need

  • 5+ years practicing employment law, with a combination of top law firm and in-house experience at a high-growth technology company

  • JD from an accredited law school and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar (New York or California preferred)

  • Deep U.S. employment counseling experience across the full employee lifecycle, including wage and hour, leaves and accommodations, investigations, performance management, and separations

  • Demonstrated ability to independently run multiple time-sensitive matters

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can turn an employment law question into guidance a manager can act on in one reading

  • High judgment on sensitive and confidential matters, and the steadiness to advise on them under time pressure

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and processes are still being built, and a bias toward action

Nice to Haves

  • Experience standing up employment infrastructure in a new country, including EOR-to-entity transitions and works council or employee representative consultation

Ramp's Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team is looking for a senior investigator ready to shift from running cases to scaling the systems that run cases. You've built real depth in TM Alerts, AML Investigations, Complex Fraud, and EDD Reviews; you know what a good escalation looks like, where analysts get stuck, and where automation actually holds up in production versus just looks good in a demo. In this role, you'll spend most of your time partnering with Engineering and the Head of FCC Tooling to turn that judgment into scaled AI systems: testing model outputs, labeling and calibrating results, and making sure every automated decision point is well-documented and properly governed. You'll stay close enough to FCC's day-to-day workflows and will partake in some of them, but this is fundamentally a builder role.

 

What You'll Do

  • Partner directly with Engineering and the Head of FCC Tooling on automation experimentation and AI initiatives across TM, sanctions, complex fraud, and EDD, moving prototypes from one-off calibration exercises to defined, repeatable evaluation processes.

  • Define and maintain test sets, scenario coverage, and evaluation frameworks for compliance AI/agent tools in partnership with the engineers building them

  • Own the documentation and governance layer for every automated or AI-assisted decision point

  • Work with the FCC team to understand current workflows to guide innovative solutions

  • Recommend automation and AI adoption decisions with evidence and escalate control-posture or model-risk trade-offs to compliance leadership

 

What You Need

  • 5+ years of financial services experience in compliance, AML, or related regulatory advisory roles, preferably in fintech

  • Demonstrated senior-investigator experience across TM Alerts, AML Investigations, Complex Fraud, and EDD Reviews

  • Direct experience testing, labeling, or evaluating AI/ML model outputs, or strong aptitude and demonstrated fast ramp-up if new to formal model evaluation

  • Strong AI fluency and data analytics skills

  • Comfort partnering with engineers day-to-day and ability to translate compliance judgment into build specs, test cases, and evaluation criteria engineers can act on

  • Strong project management and documentation rigor

  • Ability to scope an ambiguous automation problem, choose an approach, and deliver a durable outcome with minimal oversight

     

Nice-to-Haves

  • Data science background

  • Experience working with outsourced testing/QA partners on model tuning or signal collection

This is a hands-on role with executive visibility and direct impact on how Ramp’s engineering organization scales.


You’re energized by complexity and curious about how AI can improve the way engineering teams work. You experiment with AI tools yourself, understand how they are changing software development, and bring that perspective to the programs you lead.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead large technical programs across engineering and partner teams, from infrastructure scaling to reliability and incident response.

  • Connect platform and product engineering teams, keep context flowing, surface dependencies, and drive effective execution.

  • Own programs from scoping and kickoff through delivery, measurement, and retrospective.

  • Partner with engineering leaders on roadmaps, identify how projects overlap or depend on one another, and keep programs aligned with organizational goals.

  • Help engineers, engineering managers, and partner teams communicate business and engineering priorities across the organization.

  • Strengthen Ramp’s incident response program by improving processes, facilitating retrospectives, and helping teams act on what they learn.

  • Help define how TPMs work at Ramp by setting standards, creating playbooks, and improving program practices.

What You’ll Need

  • 5+ years of technical program management experience, ideally in a high-growth startup.

  • Hands-on fluency with AI tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, and a point of view on how they can improve day-to-day work and software development.

  • The ability to execute directly while improving how the broader team works.

  • A track record of building trust quickly and working effectively across teams.

  • A BA/BS in computer science, engineering, information systems, analytics, or another technical or analytical field.

  • Strong systems thinking: you can connect architecture, product, compliance, and timelines, and spot risks early.

  • Experience leading cross-functional programs toward ambitious goals with urgency and ownership.

Nice To Haves

  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure, CI/CD, or observability tools.

  • Experience leading reliability programs.

About the Role

As a Product Operations partner for Ramp Procurement, you will help build and scale the workflows that enable customers to manage their procurement processes with speed, accuracy, and control. You will improve both the requester and approver experience while shaping product quality through data, customer feedback, and tight partnership with customer-facing internal teams.

Beyond your product vertical, you will also contribute to Product Operations process improvement and product building that allows our Product and Engineering teams to scale. You will use AI tools to improve release management, collect customer feedback, and enable internal teams to support customers and troubleshoot issues.

Our main goal is to reduce customer friction, measured by support tickets per active user and customer NPS.

*Please note that this Product Operations role will require you to be comfortable with working in-person at our NYC HQ (located near Madison Square Park) at least 2 days/week*

What You’ll Do

  • Own the voice-of-customer loop for Procurement — systematically capture, analyze, and prioritize feedback from CX, Sales, and direct customer channels

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to translate customer feedback into actionable product requirements and specs

  • Own launch operations for new Procurement features as they move from Alpha to GA, including AI-native experiences that require strong customer and internal enablement

  • Directly ship product improvements (UX fixes and paper cuts) using AI tools — owning your own backlog of customer friction reduction, not just feeding the engineering backlog

  • Use AI to automate processes and build products that enable teams to ship faster while maintaining a high quality bar

  • Build scalable operating systems for release readiness, internal enablement, supportability, and issue escalation across Procurement workflows

What You Need

  • 3+ years in product operations, product management, or a customer-facing analytical role supporting B2B SaaS; experience with procurement, intake and approval workflows, spend management, or financial operations preferred

  • Proficiency using data to size opportunities and analyze adoption, support trends, payment flow performance, and customer friction

  • Ability to translate qualitative feedback into crisp requirements and operational processes

  • Comfort working in ambiguous, technically complex spaces and driving clarity across multiple stakeholders

  • Strong problem solving, prioritization, and communication skills; bias to ship improvements quickly and measure impact

  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code) to accelerate your work and directly make product improvements

About Our Teams

  • Spend Management owns our core spend product, including card issuance, reimbursements, and travel & entertainment to control spend

  • Procurement owns streamlining new purchase requests, approvals, vendors, savings, and price intelligence products to help companies make better financial decisions

  • Intelligence owns the reporting, savings, and price intelligence products to help companies make better financial decisions

  • Bill Payments owns our invoice management, accounts payable, and B2B payment capabilities

  • Risk owns our underwriting and financial products that determine which businesses to approve and how to manage risk

  • Growth owns onboarding, activation and retention products to help our customers be successful on the Ramp platform

  • Accounting owns creating intelligence in our accounting platform, saving finance teams time and money

  • Mobile owns our mobile app development and mobile strategy

This is a leadership individual contributor role. You can take any idea from zero to one. You understand the business fundamentals, the product value, the channels that perform best, and you know where brand design amplifies and improves the work. You understand each XFN’s accountability and outcomes, from product, marketing, GTM, growth and beyond. You can speak their language.

What You'll Do

  • Set creative direction. Turn business goals and audience insights into clear ideas for the brand.

  • Lead company-defining projects. Take campaigns, launches, and other brand experiences from an open question to finished work.

  • Set the bar for quality and taste. You are the go-to expert for typography, imagery, layout, and brand design. You are the champion for this standard.

  • Build the brand system. Evolve our visual identity over time. We believe in coherency over consistency. We built our brand system to behave like jazz.

  • Connect brand and product. Work with product, marketing, and engineering so the company feels coherent wherever people experience it.

  • Raise the quality of the team’s work. You are a player-coach that can mentor others and develop a culture of collaboration, creativity, and trust.

  • Tell stories to drive alignment. Help partners understand the thinking, agree on a direction, and make practical choices about scope and timing.

What makes you stand out

  • You’re already using AI tooling and agents to explore faster, iterate sooner, and develop ideas that you couldn’t before.

  • You have both agency and in-house experience.

  • You have side hobbies exploring design and creativity. We want to see side projects that show a desire for learning, a student-like mindset, and above all, enthusiasm for where the future is headed.

  • You’re humble, thoughtful, and self-aware.

  • Your portfolio reveals a story about how you’ve grown as a person, your interests, and curiosities.

  • The ability to negotiate, compromise, or understand trade-offs with executives and XFN partners.

  • The ability to connect creative choices to the audience, the product, and the business.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is redefining how businesses manage their finances, and our growth marketing team is how millions of businesses first hear that story. As we expand internationally, paid ads are one of our highest-leverage channels — and localized, high-craft creative is what makes them work in a new market.

Based in our London office, you'll own the creative that powers Ramp's international acquisition engine across Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, and Direct Mail. You'll take the playbook we've built in the US and adapt it for the UK and EU — shaping how Ramp shows up across paid social, video, and display for international audiences. You'll work closely with our Performance Marketing team to turn ideas into ads that move metrics, while pushing the creative bar on what a finance brand can look and feel like abroad.

This is a temporary full-time role, based in London.

What You'll Do

  • Design and animate paid creative end-to-end across static and motion formats, tailored for international markets.

  • Create and localize ads for Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, and emerging channels across the UK and EU.

  • Adapt the US growth creative playbook for international audiences — and flag where local nuance means it needs to break, not just translate.

  • Develop scalable design and motion systems that help the team move faster while maintaining a high creative bar.

  • Concept hooks, headlines, visual treatments, and creative variants that earn attention and drive performance in-market.

  • Partner closely with Performance Marketing, copywriters, and product marketers (largely US-based) to bring ideas to life across time zones.

  • Iterate quickly based on performance data and contribute to international testing strategy.

  • Build templates, automations, AI workflows, and creative systems that increase team velocity.

  • Explore new tools, techniques, and AI-native workflows to expand what's possible inside our production pipeline.

  • Help evolve how Ramp's brand shows up across international growth marketing.

What You Need

  • 5+ years of experience in visual design, motion design, or creative production

About Ramp

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Corporate Paralegal to join Ramp's Legal team and own the operational backbone of how we govern and structure the company. Ramp runs a growing portfolio of U.S. and non-U.S. entities — including regulated and licensed subsidiaries — across a business that ships constantly and raises, acquires, and expands on short notice. You will be the person who keeps that machinery accurate, current, and audit-ready.

This is a broad generalist role. You'll sit at the center of corporate governance, entity management, equity administration, and litigation/employment and you'll partner directly with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Compliance, Equity Admin, and People, and outside counsel. We are a small, high-leverage team supporting a company that moves quickly, so you'll cover a lot of ground and be trusted to run matters independently.

What You'll Do

  • Corporate governance: Prepare board and stockholder meeting materials, agendas, minutes, written consents, resolutions, secretary's certificates, and incumbency certificates. Track and calendar governance obligations across the entity portfolio.

  • Entity management: Own the full lifecycle of entity administration — formations and dissolutions, foreign qualifications, annual reports, franchise tax filings, registered agent management, signatories, officer and director lists, post-integration cleanup.

  • KYC, UBO, and diligence: Respond to KYC/UBO and diligence requests from bank partners, regulators, auditors, insurers, and counterparties, and build reusable packages.

  • Equity support: Support equity administration, option and RSU grants, board approvals of equity awards, secondaries, and equity plan recordkeeping in partnership with Finance and People.

  • Transaction support: Run diligence support, signature collection, closing checklists, closing binders, and post-closing obligations for financings, credit facilities, M&A, real estate, and insurance renewals.

  • Commercial and cross-functional support: Assist with powers of attorney, delegations of authority, and corporate approvals needed by the business.

  • Employment support: Support employment- and immigration-related requests and filings.

  • Litigation support: Support subpoena and law enforcement requests, legal holds, e-discovery, and document production. Review and respond to garnishment orders and UCC liens. Serve as Ramp’s custodian of records and as Ramp’s representative in small claims court cases.

What You Need

  • 6+ years of corporate paralegal experience at a major law firm and/or in-house at a high-growth technology or financial services company.

  • Deep working knowledge of corporate governance, entity formation and maintenance, corporate recordkeeping, and secretary's office functions.

  • Excellent drafting skills across resolutions, consents, certificates, and corporate documentation, with genuine precision — you catch the wrong entity name, the stale date, and the missing signature block.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently run multiple time-sensitive workstreams without dropping threads or waiting to be asked.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the judgment to work directly with executives, board members, outside counsel, and cross-functional partners.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and processes are still being built — and a bias toward action.

  • High judgment around confidential and sensitive corporate information.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a fintech, payments, or regulated financial services company, including support for licensed entities (money transmitter, EMI, or similar).

  • Experience supporting venture financings, secondaries, M&A integration, or IPO readiness.

  • International entity management experience across EMEA, APAC, LATAM, or Canada.

  • Experience with equity administration and cap table platforms (e.g., Shareworks).

  • Experiencing with litigation or employment matters.

  • Notary Public commission (NY or CA), or willingness to obtain one.

  • ABA-approved paralegal certificate.

  • A track record of using AI or automation to eliminate manual legal work.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:
