About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

  • Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

What You'll Do

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach: you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes.

Day to day, you will:

  • Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership.

  • Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered.

  • Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

  • Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

  • Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

  • Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

  • Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

  • Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

  • Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

  • Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

What We Look For

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

  • You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems.

  • You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage.

  • You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen.

  • You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code.

  • You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

  • You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

  • You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

  • You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

  • You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

  • You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including a track record of shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems.

  • Staff+-level technical leadership: experience setting technical direction and leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives from ambiguous problems through durable production outcomes.

  • Experience managing, mentoring, and developing engineers. You create clarity, give direct feedback, and help people grow in technical judgment, scope, and leadership.

  • A sustained hands-on engineering track record. You are comfortable writing and reviewing production code, evaluating system designs, debugging incidents, and making difficult technical tradeoffs.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating distributed systems at production scale.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code and set that standard for the team.

  • Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred).

  • Familiarity with observability and reliability practices, including SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards, and incident response.

  • Track record of delivering through cross-functional coordination: aligning stakeholders, unblocking teams, and staying accountable for the outcome.

  • Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — and helping a team use them to move faster and think bigger.

Bonus (not required):

  • Experience with cellular or multi-tenant architecture patterns

  • Prior work on workflow orchestration systems (Temporal)

  • Contributions to developer experience or internal platform tooling

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or regulated industries (FedRAMP, SOC 2)

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

You will set the operating rhythm for complex pre-sales work, coach the team on discovery, solution design, demos, technical deal strategy, and partner closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Account Management to deliver a cohesive customer experience.

You will remain close to high-impact opportunities while scaling the team’s technical ownership financial fluency, and executive presence. This is a player-coach leadership role: you will improve how the team qualifies and advances complex opportunities, create repeatable practices and assets, and use customer insight to shape Ramp’s go-to-market and product priorities.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Enterprise Solutions Consultants; set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, and support career growth.

  • Establish a high-quality operating cadence for pipeline reviews, deal strategy, forecasting, staffing, and performance management.

  • Partner with Enterprise Sales leadership to shape account strategy, qualify complex opportunities, and deploy the right solutions resources at the right moments.

  • Coach the team to lead discovery, deliver tailored demos, and architect solutions that connect Ramp’s platform, financial workflows, ERP systems, and integrations to customer priorities.

  • Engage directly in the most strategic or complex customer situations, including executive conversations, technical validation, RFPs, and escalations.

  • Build scalable playbooks, technical assets, demo standards, and knowledge-sharing practices that improve quality and consistency across the team.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, Customer Success, and Services to translate recurring customer needs into actionable feedback, roadmap context, and strong handoffs.

  • Define and inspect team health metrics such as coverage, conversion, cycle efficiency, solution quality, customer outcomes, and talent development.

  • Foster an inclusive, high-accountability culture grounded in customer empathy, strong collaboration, speed, and continuous improvement.

  • Identify practical ways for the team to use AI to improve preparation, documentation, solutioning, and customer-facing work while maintaining quality and good judgment.

What You Need

  • 8+ years of experience in Solutions Consulting, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Professional Services, or a related customer-facing technical role, including 3+ years of people management or demonstrated player-coach leadership.

  • Proven success leading teams through complex enterprise sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders, technical requirements, and long decision processes.

  • Strong understanding of enterprise financial operations, controllership priorities, and accounting workflows.

  • Working fluency with enterprise systems and integrations, including ERP platforms such as NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or Microsoft Dynamics; APIs; SFTP; and adjacent HRIS, identity, and security systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to coach others on discovery, solution design, executive storytelling, technical communication, and consultative selling.

  • Strong operating judgment: able to prioritize limited resources, inspect pipeline health, make trade-offs, and drive execution in a fast-moving environment.

  • Executive presence and ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders by translating technical complexity into business value.

  • Track record of building repeatable processes, assets, and team rituals that elevate performance beyond individual contributions.

  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows for solutions, sales, or customer-facing teams.

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and change-management skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting fintech, spend management, accounting automation, or other financial software products.

  • Familiarity with government or public-sector selling.

  • Familiarity with Python, Java, or SQL; data integration and ETL platforms; cloud infrastructure; or enterprise authentication and security protocols.

  • Flexible PTO

  • One Medical annual membership

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

You'll lead a group of 6-8 Account Managers, each carrying a book of 60-70 Enterprise customers with real latitude over how they grow it. This is a build role, not a maintain role: the playbooks, coaching systems, and performance bar you set are the ones this team runs on next year. Your ceiling is set by how well you turn individual AM judgment into a repeatable, scalable motion that grows the segment.

What You'll Do

  • Build and run a high-performing team of 6-8 Account Managers - setting the bar for culture, morale, and daily execution.

  • Get embedded in the relationships that matter. Engage directly with key customers and top accounts alongside your team, building trust and long-term partnership.

  • Own the number. Manage quota performance and pipeline generation across your team to hit spend activation, product activation, retention, and expansion goals.

  • Forecast and report team performance to senior leadership with clear-eyed visibility into what's working and what isn't.

  • Hire and develop the next generation of AMs - training on product, buyer personas, competition, and tooling through role-plays, game film, and real deal work.

  • Coach relentlessly. Run daily 1:1s, dissect call feedback, lead enablement sessions, and build career paths for every rep on your team.

  • Turn what works into a system. Continuously refine team processes and tooling to improve output and efficiency as the segment scales.

  • Represent Account Management cross-functionally, partnering with Sales, CX, CSM, Risk, and Product to remove blockers and drive outcomes.

What You Need

  • Minimum 5 years of quota-carrying sales or account management experience as an individual contributor, with a proven, consistent track record of exceeding goals (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory)

  • Minimum 5 years building and leading account management or sales teams, with a track record of exceeding goal (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory)

  • Prior success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS or AI companies

  • A genuine passion for hiring, with a thoughtful approach to talent development

  • Ability to articulate contractual, technical, and financial value to customers, including C-Suite and executive leaders

  • Strong track record negotiating, structuring, and executing complex agreements

  • Proficiency with data analytics tools (Salesforce, Looker, Excel) and a bias toward using data to drive decisions

  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills, backed by excellent communication and presentation ability.

  • High agency and adaptability - no two days are the same, and the only constant is change

  • A desire and willingness to jump headfirst into complex, challenging problems for the good of the business.

Great to Haves

  • Experience at a high-growth, top SaaS/AI startup

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

As the Manager, Mid-Market Solutions at Ramp, you will lead and develop a high-performing team of Solutions Consultants supporting Mid-Market prospects and customers. You will establish the operating rhythm for a high-volume, fast-moving pre-sales motion; coach the team on discovery, demos, solution fit, and value-based selling; and partner closely with Sales, Product, Customer Success, Account Management, and Technical Consulting to deliver a consistent customer experience.

You will stay close to important opportunities while building a scalable team model: clear engagement standards, repeatable demos and discovery practices, strong capacity planning, and effective handoffs. You will use customer feedback and performance data to improve how Mid-Market Solutions Consultants help Ramp win, activate, and grow customers.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Mid-Market Solutions Consultants; set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, and support career growth.

  • Partner with Mid-Market Sales leadership to improve qualification, deploy Solutions capacity effectively, and build repeatable account and deal strategies.

  • Coach the team to run high-quality discovery, deliver tailored and efficient demos, connect Ramp’s products to finance and accounting workflows, and navigate solution-fit conversations with confidence.

  • Personally support the highest-priority or most complex Mid-Market opportunities, escalations, and customer-facing moments when needed.

  • Build scalable playbooks, demo standards, discovery frameworks, enablement assets, and knowledge-sharing practices that raise the team’s quality and speed.

  • Partner with Product, Product Marketing, Customer Success, Account Management, and Technical Consulting to translate recurring customer needs into clear feedback, strong handoffs, and improved customer outcomes.

  • Define and inspect team health metrics such as coverage, conversion, cycle efficiency, demo quality, solution fit, customer outcomes, and talent development.

  • Foster an inclusive, high-accountability culture grounded in customer empathy, collaboration, urgency, and continuous improvement.

  • Identify practical ways for the team to use AI to improve preparation, documentation, deal research, demo readiness, and customer-facing work while maintaining good judgment.

What You Need

  • 6+ years of experience in Solutions Consulting, Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Professional Services, or a related customer-facing technical role, including 2+ years of people management or demonstrated player-coach leadership.

  • Proven success leading or mentoring teams in a high-volume SaaS, fintech, or other customer-facing commercial environment.

  • Strong understanding of financial operations, accounting workflows, and the needs of finance and operations stakeholders.

  • Working knowledge of business systems and integrations, including ERP, HRIS, identity, or accounting platforms; APIs and file-based integrations are a plus.

  • Demonstrated ability to coach others on discovery, solution fit, demo execution, commercial judgment, technical communication, and consultative selling.

  • Strong operating judgment: able to prioritize team capacity, inspect pipeline health, use data to improve execution, and make clear trade-offs in a fast-paced environment.

  • Proven ability to partner effectively with Sales and post-sales leaders while protecting customer trust and delivery readiness.

  • Track record of building repeatable team processes, assets, and rituals that improve consistency beyond individual contributions.

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and change-management skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, spend management, accounting automation, payments, or adjacent financial software.

  • Familiarity with Ramp-relevant systems such as ERP, HRIS, identity, or accounting platforms.

  • Experience using AI-assisted workflows to improve solutions, sales, or customer-facing team effectiveness.

About the Role

People Programs at Ramp builds the programs that shape how employees experience the company day to day; from someone's first week to the moments that define Ramp's culture company-wide. As Ramp scales, we need someone dedicated to building that function and taking our foundations to the next level.

In this role, you'll own programs like onboarding, manager enablement, engagement surveys, and the company-wide culture and recognition programs that shape how Ramp works, to name a few. You'll work closely with People Business Partners, People Operations, and Comms to make these programs land and thrive.

This work is high impact and high visibility. This is a hands-on, build-from-scratch role for someone with strong judgment who owns things fully.

What You'll Do

  • Build your own roadmap by pulling signal from engagement survey results, PBP and manager input, and People Ops, then make the call on what to build, improve, delegate, or stop.

  • Own onboarding effectiveness — from pre-start through the first week — so every new hire's first experience of Ramp reflects how we work and our culture, partnering with People Ops and IT on day-to-day logistics

  • Own the performance review cycle's program design — timeline, tools, and the manager/employee experience — partnering with PBPs on calibration and outcomes

  • Build and own manager enablement as a standalone program: design the content, frameworks, and moments that help managers lead well, in partnership with PBPs on delivery

  • Conceive, build, and run company-wide culture-building programs, fully owning logistics and content end-to-end

  • Own recognition programming: how we surface and celebrate what's worth celebrating across the company and the rituals/milestones that make Ramp's culture tangible day to day

  • Own the biannual engagement survey: design, run, and work with People Business Partners to translate results into action

  • Be the trusted voice on what we should build in-house versus buy (tools, vendors, platforms) for people programs, grounded in judgment about what's worth the investment, not a default toward either

What You Need

  • 5+ years owning people/culture programs end-to-end at a high-growth company - from ideation through hands-on execution

  • A builder's track record: you've created programming that didn't exist before, not adapted someone else's playbook

  • Strong facilitation and executive presence. You’re comfortable being the face of a program in front of the whole company, not just behind the scenes

  • Comfortable with data: you can read engagement survey results and program metrics and turn them into a point of view, not just a report

  • Proven ability to partner across functions (PBPs, Comms, Enablement, leadership)

  • First-principles thinker who can turn ambiguity into a scalable framework: you don't need a rule book, but you can build one when it's missing

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

About the Role

Ramp is hiring a Brand Partnerships Manager to shape and accelerate our growth through strategic partnerships and collaborations.

You’ll build our brand partnerships strategy from the ground up: sourcing high-potential partners, developing relationships, structuring creative collaborations, and turning them into campaigns that drive awareness, engagement, and business growth.

Success in this role looks like building real, high-impact partnerships with tangible value for Ramp, our partners, and the audiences we reach together. The ideal candidate is a marketer who can also run a deal: you come up with the partnership, you know why it matters for the business, and you execute relentlessly to get it out the door. You should have an instinct for great ideas, a strong creative point of view, and a close read on what’s happening across media, sports, and culture. Most importantly, you’ve turned those ideas into campaigns that break through culture, get attention, and drive business outcomes.

Ramp is a place for people who move fast, take ownership, and are looking to do the best work of their careers. We want someone who can build this function out, bet on partners that matter, and create collaborations that move the needle and are unmistakably Ramp.

What You'll Do

  • Own Ramp’s brand partnerships program end to end: partner strategy, sourcing, negotiation, and execution.

  • Find high-value partners across finance, sports, business, and media who can put Ramp in front of new audiences.

  • Build a system for spotting and tracking emerging talent so we can place smart bets early. We sponsored Neal Shipley while he was still an amateur golfer, and TBPN in the very early days. We like spotting emerging brands and talent before everyone else does.

  • Develop bold partnership concepts that tie into Ramp’s brand, product priorities, launches, and broader marketing campaigns.

  • Lead deal strategy and negotiation, including pricing, asset packages, usage rights, exclusivity, deliverables, timelines, and contract terms.

  • Work with teams across Ramp to run and test campaigns across paid, owned, and earned channels, so every partnership delivers both creative impact and business results.

  • Manage active partnerships day to day. Keep deliverables on track, and keep finding new ways to work with existing partners so Ramp gets the most out of every relationship.

  • Work closely with Ramp’s sales team to spot deals where a partner could help, and find timely, relevant ways to bring them in.

  • Handle reporting for every partnership. Track delivery and performance, share what you’re learning, and recommend when to renew, expand, change, or end a deal.

What You Need

  • 5+ years of experience in brand marketing, influencer marketing, partnerships, or a related role.

  • A track record of developing, negotiating, and executing high-profile brand, media, or strategic partnerships, ideally within a fast moving in-house team or at an agency. The ideal candidate has a builder mindset and is willing to challenge conventional approaches and take a first principles approach.

  • Strong creative judgment, with the ability to spot culturally relevant ideas and turn them into partnerships and campaigns that earn attention.

  • The ability to thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and launch new programs quickly from scratch You can move from strategy to execution quickly, manage complexity, and drive work across teams.

  • Excel at balancing brand authenticity with performance metrics. Strong business acumen and judgment to balance efficiency with bold bets.

  • Ability to switch between strategy and in-the-weeds execution. In one meeting, you’re zooming out to set the vision and framework, the next you’re diving into day-to-day execution and delivery.

  • A strong interest in culture, entertainment, and sports.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

Ramp is hiring a Lead Recruiter to own Director-level and above hiring across our G&A and business functions. You will lead some of the company’s most critical leadership searches, partnering directly with senior stakeholders to identify and hire leaders who will shape Ramp’s next stage of growth.

You will own searches from initial scoping through close, partnering directly with executives and senior leaders across the business. You will be expected to develop real fluency in each area you support, translate ambiguous business needs into clear hiring strategies, and bring an independent point of view on talent.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally strong at research, assessment, stakeholder partnership, and closing. You should be comfortable challenging assumptions, navigating sensitive and confidential searches, and creating structure without slowing the business down. You should be a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, builds pipelines from scratch, and takes ownership of moving searches forward even when the role, target profile, or process is still taking shape.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for Director-level and above roles across G&A and business functions, from intake and market mapping through offer and close.

  • Develop real fluency in the functions you support and quickly build context when taking on a new area, so you can identify the signals that distinguish exceptional leaders beyond title, company, and tenure.

  • Build proactive pipelines through market research, targeted sourcing, referrals, and thoughtful engagement with passive candidates. Independently build momentum on confidential searches where broad outreach or an existing pipeline may not be available.

  • Develop assessment approaches that surface a candidate’s leadership effectiveness, functional expertise, and ability to operate at Ramp’s pace and scale.

  • Move fluidly across functions, evolving role definitions, and competing priorities while maintaining a consistently high bar for talent, execution, and candidate experience.

  • Exercise discretion throughout sensitive searches, managing candidate information and stakeholder communication with sound judgment.

 

What You Need

  • 6+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience.

  • A track record of independently leading complex senior-level searches from initial scoping through accepted offer.

  • Ability to advise senior leaders, challenge requirements, and influence hiring decisions through clear communication, market insight, and data.

  • Demonstrated ability to build fluency in unfamiliar functions, context-switch across very different searches, and maintain strong judgment as priorities and scope change.

  • A high level of ownership and comfort with ambiguity. You can turn an open-ended business need into an actionable search, build a pipeline from scratch, and drive progress without waiting for direction.

  • Strong closing skills, including experience navigating competing offers, senior candidates, and sensitive searches.

     

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior experience in executive search or a dedicated leadership recruiting role, particularly across G&A or business functions.

  • Experience partnering directly with CEOs or other C-suite leaders on critical hires.

  • Experience improving interview architecture, scorecards, market maps, or recruiting processes where structure was limited or still being built.

  • Experience developing AI-enabled recruiting workflows that were adopted beyond your own individual searches.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Getting paid is still one of the most manual parts of running a business. Finance teams chase invoices over email, match payments to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and close the books late because cash data is scattered across banks, payment processors, and ERPs.

Ramp's Accounts Receivable team is building the system that automates all of it, from the moment an invoice is sent to the moment cash is reconciled in the general ledger. We own the full receivables lifecycle: invoicing, collections, payments, cash application, and accounting sync.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own core pieces of that system. The work sits where hard engineering problems meet real money: matching messy payment data to the right invoices, keeping ledgers correct to the cent, and syncing reliably with the accounting systems our customers depend on. You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.


What You’ll Do

  • Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

  • Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

  • Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

  • Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

  • Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

  • Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

What You’ll Need

  • Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push back when the spec is wrong

  • Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

  • Strong system design judgment and the ability to balance speed, correctness, reliability, and simplicity

  • A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to technical decisions

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, or other financial workflows

  • Experience building integrations that keep data consistent across systems

  • Experience improving reliability and operational visibility in a growing product

You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.

 - Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

 - Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

 - Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

 - Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

 - Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 - Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

 - Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

About the Role

Ramp's SMB sales team runs a high-velocity, full-cycle sales motion. We sell Ramp's full platform (corporate cards, expense management, bill pay, and procurement) to businesses with up to 150 employees, working with their founders, CEOs, and finance leaders.

In this role, you'll help small businesses find a better way to manage their spend and run their finances. You'll own each customer relationship from the first conversation through close: learning how the business operates today, uncovering what's slowing the team down, and showing how Ramp solves it. It's a fast-moving seat with a lot of customer conversations, so you'll sharpen your discovery and closing craft quickly and see your impact in every customer you bring on.

This is a role for a seller who has done the work at both ends of the funnel: someone who started their sales career as an SDR, earned a closing seat, and wants a much bigger volume of at-bats. You'll get coaching, a team that shares what works, and clear paths to grow into Commercial sales, Ramp's newer AI product teams, account management, or leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full sales cycle for SMB customers, from discovery and demo through pricing, negotiation, and close.

  • Run 10–12 customer conversations a day while keeping a clean, accurate pipeline and forecast.

  • Close at high volume (the team expects 50–60 new customers a month per rep once ramped).

  • Self-source part of your business through daily outbound (about 10% of your closed-won customers).

  • Run focused discovery with founders, CEOs, and finance leaders, and connect Ramp to the pain they describe.

  • Learn Ramp's products and internal tools quickly, and adapt as products and workflows change.

What You Need

  • 2–3 years of combined sales experience, including at least one year in a quota-carrying, closing AE role.

  • A start in sales development (SDR or BDR) or another outbound role, with a track record of self-sourcing pipeline.

  • Experience selling SaaS or tech, ideally a product similar to Ramp.

  • A track record as a top performer against quota.

  • Comfort leading pricing and negotiation conversations.

  • Strong organization: you can prioritize a large book of deals and keep each one moving.

  • Comfort with change and ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-intensity environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling to executive buyers such as CFOs, CEOs, or directors of finance.

  • Familiarity with finance or Office of the CFO topics (we'll coach this).

  • Experience managing a pipeline in Gong or a similar deal board with forecast categories.

    • Own customer and operational outcomes. Take responsibility for a defined problem, establish a baseline, and follow through until the experience improves.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is scaling fast in the UK. Our European operations team (Europs) gets UK and EU businesses onboarded across Ramp's own regulated entities and our card-issuing and payments partners. We're a small team that runs on frontier AI tooling: our operators build and maintain their own automations and apps, and have taken daily processes from hours to minutes. We're hiring a KYB Operations Lead to run the UK onboarding operation day to day. You'll manage our UK operators, own the queue, make the hard calls on complex cases and escalations, and keep improving how the operation works as volume grows. This is a hands-on leadership role: you'll be as comfortable in a difficult ownership structure as in a capacity plan.

What You'll Do

  • Line-manage and develop the UK operators: prioritisation, 1:1s, performance, and helping them grow as builders as well as reviewers

  • Own overall queue management and resourcing for UK onboarding: what gets worked first, who works it, and how we keep cases moving through leave and spikes in volume

  • Make the final first-line (1LoD) call on complex cases: complex ownership structures, EDD, PEP and adverse-media outcomes, and cases that need a judgement rather than a checklist

  • Own escalations with our card-issuing and payments partners, including recurring failures, disputed or unnecessary requirements, and turning each fix into a repeatable playbook

  • Run customer-facing onboarding communications with quality: clear requests, fast follow-ups, no avoidable back-and-forth

  • Define and report operational metrics (caseload by provider, time to close, handling time) and use them to improve the operation

  • Find and remove friction: spot requirements customers shouldn't have to meet twice and work with Product and Engineering to design them out

  • Build consistent, evidenced 1LoD decision standards that hold up to partner sample reviews and second-line scrutiny

  • Act as hands-on backup for UK safeguarding: daily reconciliations and investigating breaks when cover is needed

What You Need

  • 5+ years in KYB / onboarding / financial-crime operations at a UK fintech, EMI, PI or bank

  • Practical working knowledge of the UK regulatory framework for EMIs/PIs: MLRs 2017, JMLSG guidance, and FCA expectations for customer due diligence

  • Strong judgement on complex business customers: multi-layer ownership, overseas parents, trusts, PEPs, and knowing when to escalate

  • Clear written communication, both with customers and in documented case decisions

  • Demonstrated use of AI tools in your day-to-day work to go faster or do better work, with concrete examples

  • A bias to fix the process rather than just work the queue

 

Nice-to-Haves

  • Line management of operators or analysts (strongly preferred)

  • Experience working with card-issuing, BaaS or payments partners on onboarding (e.g. partner due-diligence requests, sample reviews)

  • Safeguarding / client-money reconciliation experience

  • Writing requirements for Product and Engineering teams

  • EU onboarding experience or a second European language

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About the Role

Ramp is hiring a People Business Partner to support managers and employees across Marketing, Finance, Legal, People, Talent, Workplace, and Executive Assistants. Reporting to the Lead People Business Partner for Business & G&A, you’ll be the primary People Business contact for these teams. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: one day you may coach an employee through a difficult conversation, and the next you may partner with a C-suite executive on a major reorganization. No task is too big or too small. You’ll build a sustainable network across employees, managers, and leaders so you deeply understand each team’s work, talent, and business goals. You’ll independently own the People Business agenda for this portfolio, including its most senior leaders: set priorities with them, shape consequential talent and organizational changes, and drive the work through implementation and results.

What You'll Do

  • Own the People Business agenda for your portfolio. Build trusted relationships across employees, managers, and senior leaders; understand each team’s business goals, talent, and challenges; and set priorities that deliver results.

  • Improve how managers manage. Coach managers through performance, feedback, development, retention, and difficult talent decisions. Help employees prepare for difficult conversations, and partner with senior leaders to strengthen management across their teams.

  • Drive talent and organizational changes. Use firsthand context and people data to diagnose needs, align leaders on trade-offs, and lead work such as team redesign, leadership development or hiring, and new performance approaches through implementation and measurable results.

  • Own sensitive people matters. Manage intake, communication, and follow-through for employee relations, leave, accommodations, investigations, and other cases, partnering with People Operations, Legal, Immigration, and other specialists.

  • Lead performance, engagement, and compensation work. Guide teams through twice-yearly reviews and engagement cycles, including manager preparation, calibration, and follow-up. Advise leaders on cash and equity rewards through partnerships with the Compensation team.

  • Make the wider People Business team more effective. Identify recurring gaps, build reusable processes, guidance, or tools, drive adoption, and measure improvements in quality, consistency, or capacity.

What You Need

  • A strong record of improving how managers manage, including direct coaching on performance, development, retention, and difficult talent decisions. Relevant experience may come from People Business Partner work, consulting, leadership development, or substantial management experience.

  • Sound talent judgment and independent ownership. You can earn senior-leader trust, set priorities across a broad portfolio, and drive consequential people and organizational changes through implementation with limited direction.

  • Good judgment in sensitive situations. You act decisively with incomplete information, communicate clearly, maintain confidentiality and documentation, and know when to involve specialists or escalate with a recommendation.

  • Strong analytical habits. You use people and business data alongside firsthand context to identify priorities, recommend practical action, and assess results.

  • A hands-on IC mindset. You enjoy detailed casework and direct employee and manager coaching alongside senior-leader partnership. If your background is outside HR, you can learn People policies and case processes quickly with coaching.

Nice to Have

  • Prior People Business Partner experience, including employee relations, compensation, and recurring performance and engagement cycles.

  • Experience in people consulting, performance coaching, or learning and development that includes direct work with managers and measurable talent outcomes.

  • Experience creating reusable manager guidance, case templates, or responsible AI and automation workflows that improve a People team’s effectiveness.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking a 2LoD Compliance Strategist to provide dedicated independent second-line assurance across Ramp UK & Irish regulated businesses.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can turn regulatory expectations into a practical, evidence-led monitoring and assurance programme.

The role sits within Ramp's Europe Compliance function and supports the Head of Compliance & MLRO - Europe. You will not own first-line operational decisions or perform routine casework. Instead, you will independently test and challenge the design and operation of financial-crime, safeguarding, payments, outsourcing, governance, and regulatory-change controls. You will make sure that findings are understood, remediated by accountable owners, and independently validated before closure.

Ramp Payments Europe is developing across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, payment rails, banking partners, product journeys, and shared Group services. The successful candidate will help give management and Boards a clear, reliable view of whether controls work in practice and where action is needed.

What You'll Do

  • Run a practical, risk-based compliance monitoring programme across Ramps European entities.

  • Test key controls and identify gaps, with a focus on whether they work in practice.

  • Support assurance over financial-crime, payments, safeguarding, and outsourced-service controls.

  • Track regulatory, Board, partner, audit, and internal commitments to ensure actions are completed on time.

  • Manage findings and remediation, helping accountable teams resolve issues and confirming actions are closed.

  • Produce clear reporting for management and Boards on key risks, control issues, incidents, and progress.

  • Provide independent compliance input and advisory on significant product, payments, outsourcing, and operational changes.

  • Deputise for the Head of Compliance & MLRO where required.

What You Need

  • Min. 4 year of experience in compliance, risk, audit, controls, or regulatory change within payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated environment.

  • Experience supporting compliance monitoring, control testing, issue management, remediation, or governance reporting.

  • Working knowledge of UK and/or EU financial-services regulation, with the ability to apply requirements pragmatically in a fast-moving environment.

  • Familiarity with financial-crime controls such as customer due diligence, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, or record keeping.

  • An interest in areas such as payments, safeguarding, outsourcing, operational resilience, or third-party oversight.

  • Strong judgement and communication skills, with the confidence to identify issues, explain risk clearly, and work constructively with stakeholders.

  • Comfortable working independently, managing priorities, and partnering with Product, Engineering, Operations, Legal, and Risk teams.

  • Curious about using AI responsibly to improve compliance analysis, monitoring, or documentation.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in a UK payment institution, e-money institution, bank, card issuer, acquiring business, or payments fintech.

  • Experience supporting FCA-facing work, banking-partner due diligence requirements.

  • Experience with Consumer Duty, safeguarding, or formal outsourcing governance.

  • Professional compliance, audit, risk, or financial-crime qualification.

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

About the Role

Ramp is building the Private Equity channel into one of the company's most significant sources of enterprise growth. Sponsors and their operating teams shape how portfolio companies run finance, and when they standardize on a platform, they do it across dozens of companies at once.

This role will be focused on managing the largest funds in the market. You will own a book of the most strategic PE firms Ramp works with, many of which have multiple investment investment strategies, fund vehicles, and GP stakes businesses under a single name. Each one likely has a different operating partner for each strategy, a deal team with its own relationships, and portfolio CFOs who make the final call. Your job is to know all of them, keep every thread moving, and turn that access into measurable adoption across their portfolios.

It is a high-volume, high-stakes book. The work is relentless relationship management paired with genuine commercial discipline, and it carries the highest CP goal on the channel team. There are only a handful of these seats at Ramp, and real executive visibility comes with them.

What You'll Do

  • Own a book of upmarket and megafund PE partners, serving as their primary relationship owner at Ramp.

  • Multi-thread across each firm: operating partners by strategy, deal teams, platform and portfolio operations leaders, and portfolio-company CFOs.

  • Run disciplined portfolio analysis to find where Ramp can create value, and work with Account Executives to convert that into pipeline.

  • Generate and own qualified pipeline against an aggressive CP target, prioritizing the large opportunities that move the number.

  • Negotiate custom partnership structures where they make sense, including adoption commitments, and hold the line where terms do not work for Ramp.

  • Partner with Events, Growth, Marketing, and Finance to deliver sponsorships, webinars, executive dinners and the collateral your partners ask for.

  • Build and maintain the operating system behind the book: relationship maps, portfolio analysis, follow-ups and next steps across a large partner set on a tight touch cycle

  • Use AI to automate research, portfolio mapping, call prep and follow-through so the book scales beyond what manual effort allows

What You Need

  • A track record of carrying and hitting a high quota in a commercial role. Outbound sales development, account executive, or partnerships backgrounds all work.

  • Deep working knowledge of how a private equity firm is structured, including the distinct roles of operating partners, deal teams, and portfolio leadership.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and expand relationships across a large, complex organization.

  • Exceptional organization and agency. History of managing a large book without dropping threads, continual follow-up, and navigating complex organizations.

  • Comfort negotiating directly with sophisticated counterparts, and the judgment to know when to walk away.

  • A practical, self-directed approach to AI. You build your own workflows rather than waiting for tooling.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts across events, growth, marketing and finance. Ability to work dynamically with others internally to drive results.

  • Willingness to travel frequently and to work from our New York office. CT or NJ with an in-office commitment also works, and we are open to relocation

Nice to Haves

  • Experience partnering with or selling to private equity firms and their portfolio companies.

  • Experience at a company with an established channel sales motion.

  • Fintech, payments, expense management, or CFO-software background.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

Ramp is hiring Customer Activation Manager for Stack, Ramp's purpose-built AI accounting platform for accounting firms and in-house finance teams. Its agents follow each team's processes across connected systems to complete reviewable accounting work, from recurring tasks through close and reconciliations. You will help customers identify use cases, translate their accounting process into a practical implementation plan, and build trust in agentic bookkeeping through results, impact, and deployment. You will own the customer-facing path from discovery through adoption, partner with specialists on technical setup, and help shape the playbook as the product grows. This role calls for accounting judgment, experience bringing software or process change to life with customers, and an understanding of agentic workflows.

What You’ll Do

  • Learn how each customer handles close, reconciliations, journal entries, exceptions, and review today; identify where Stack and agentic workflows can deliver useful value.

  • Translate the current process into an implementation plan with clear inputs, owners, dependencies, validation steps, and human review.

  • Guide Controllers, accountants, and other stakeholders from discovery through first use, training, and repeat adoption; adjust the plan when confidence or usage stalls.

  • Coordinate with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and other Ramp teams on deployments as well as process, systems, and product improvements

  • Act as an advocate and expert on AI-assisted accounting work

  • Turn early customer learnings into reusable discovery questions, launch steps, and adoption practices for the next implementation.

What You’ll Need

  • Roughly 4+ years of relevant experience in customer success, software implementation, accounting systems implementation, finance transformation, consulting, or a related customer-facing role; level is flexible based on experience.

  • Hands-on accounting fluency: you can explain source data, close or reconciliation steps, exceptions, controls, and sign-off with concrete examples.

  • Experience translating an accounting or finance workflow into a software implementation or process change, with evidence of what improved.

  • Ownership of customer or client adoption beyond setup, including stakeholder alignment, training, troubleshooting, and follow-through.

  • Clear communication with both finance leaders and hands-on accountants, especially when a proposed automation needs validation or a change in scope.

  • Comfort creating a plan and reusable process when the product and implementation motion are still evolving.

Nice to Haves

  • CPA, public accounting, controllership, or accounting advisory experience paired with software implementation or consulting.

  • Experience with accounting automation, close management, or forward-deployed accounting work.

  • Familiarity with ERP or accounting-system integrations and the data or permission issues that arise during implementation.

  • Experience helping accounting teams adopt AI-assisted workflows with appropriate human review.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Ramp Labs

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.

About the Role

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.

What You’ll Do

  • Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment

  • Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on

  • Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks

  • Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship

  • Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work

What You Need

  • Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions

  • Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast

  • Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise

  • Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it

  • Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces

  • Taste for what is worth measuring

Nice-to-Have

  • Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team

  • Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks

  • Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)

  • Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)

  • Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work

  • Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • One Medical annual membership

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

About the Role

This role will own the strategy and ops teams that are making that transition a reality while still delivering 24/7/365 support for our 85,000+ customers every day. You will work with the Head of CX to set the goals, measure what matters, and build the systems and programs that push the team forward. You’ll manage a small and mighty team across Business Operations, CX Analytics, Workforce Management, Learning & Development, and CX AI Operations to accomplish your goals.

We believe every CX frontline specialist has a role to play driving forward the performance of our AI agents - it is not work reserved for a dedicated AI team. Each specialist needs to be trained, coached, scheduled, and rewarded for continuous work of closing AI learning loops, ensuring AI escalations get resolved, and obsessing about how our customers are actually being served.

  • Set the goals and measure what matters. Work with the Head of CX and senior CX managers to set org-wide goals, decide how we measure progress, and deliver the programs and projects that enable that strategy to flourish.

  • Experience with production AI agents, evaluations, escalation workflows, and continuous improvement.

  • Taking an operating model that worked in one team and making it successful elsewhere.

  • Specialists and AI agents work as one team, measured through both direct frontline performance as well as agentic velocity.

  • Every specialist is trained, coached, scheduled, and rewarded for migrating successfully into an AI native version of the role.

  • Other Ramp operations teams are adopting what worked in CX.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the role

Corporate Security at Ramp owns the identity and access layer for the company: Okta, Google Workspace, the SaaS applications behind them, and the governance that decides who holds what. We are hiring a Senior Security Engineer, Identity, to turn that layer into IAM as a service — a platform the rest of Ramp can use without filing a ticket.

 

The role is hands-on. You will design how identity works at Ramp and write the code that implements it: identity configuration in Terraform, entitlements created and governed through an agentic workflow, and an on-call agent that answers access questions before anyone has to ask a person. As more access flows between applications and AI agents rather than people, you will own how those identities are issued, scoped, and audited.

 

You will report to the Corporate Security lead and work closely with IT, Security Engineering, AI DevX, and the Data team.

What you'll do

  • Own Terraform for identity services: Okta applications, authorization servers, authentication policies, groups and group rules, and SCIM provisioning

  • Design and operate custom authorization servers, including audiences, scopes, claims, and access policies for internal services and AI agents

  • Implement app-to-app and agent access through Cross App Access (XAA) and ID-JAG, so delegated access is brokered and governed by the IdP rather than granted user by user

  • Own our IGA platform: the entitlement catalog, ownership, access requests, time-bound grants, and certifications

  • Build the agentic workflow that takes a team from "I have a new group of people who need access to X" to a defined, owned, and governed entitlement, with the Terraform and IGA changes opened for review

  • Build identity graphs with ISPM tooling to target overprivileged and long-standing access across human and non-human identities

  • Build the identity data lake behind an on-call agent that can explain events like a User Not Assigned Application error in Okta before the employee opens a ticket

What you need

  • 6+ years in identity engineering or IAM, including operational ownership of Okta or an equivalent identity provider at scale

  • Deep understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM, including how custom authorization servers issue and enforce aud, scope, and claims

  • Working knowledge of how XAA and ID-JAG work under the hood, including token exchange and JWT bearer grants

  • Experience with ISPM or identity graph tooling, and turning its findings into automated remediation

  • Experience owning an IGA platform or building the equivalent in-house

  • Terraform experience managing identity providers, including module design, state, and CI

  • Programming in Python or Go, with experience building against platform APIs

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About the Role

As a member of Ramp's Fraud Operations team, you will play a pivotal role in safeguarding the company and its customers against fraudulent activities. This position involves analyzing new account applications, monetary and non-monetary account activity to identify and mitigate risks associated with first-party and third-party fraud.

We are seeking a detail-oriented professional who is adept at applying fraud detection techniques and leveraging data sources and tools to develop logical courses of action. In addition to technical acumen, this role requires strong interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively cross-functionally and with customers, external financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies. Ideal candidates are self-starters who are energized by ambiguity and love creating clarity.

What You'll Do

  • Analyze new account applications to detect potential fraud patterns, including identity theft, synthetic identities, and other high-risk behaviors.

  • Evaluate transactional activity, identifying anomalies and irregularities indicative of fraudulent behavior.

  • Thoroughly investigate alerts of first-party and third-party fraud, providing comprehensive documentation of findings.

  • Investigate and facilitate customer card disputes, ensuring cases are resolved accurately and within network timelines.

  • Use AI tools and automation to streamline investigations, and help develop and improve the processes and tooling behind them.

  • Collaborate with internal teams, such as Credit Risk, Compliance, and Customer Support, to ensure timely resolution of fraud-related issues.

  • Communicate directly with customers to verify account activity, resolve disputes, and gather necessary documentation during investigations.

  • Liaise with external stakeholders, including financial institutions and law enforcement, to support investigations and facilitate recovery efforts when necessary.

  • Stay updated on emerging fraud trends, industry best practices, and regulatory requirements to enhance fraud prevention and detection measures.

  • Perform root cause analyses, document control breakdowns, and work with the strategy and engineering teams to improve fraud controls.

  • Document procedures and proactively identify opportunities for operational process improvement.

Work Schedule Requirements

Fraud doesn't operate on a standard 9-to-5 schedule, and neither does this role. Candidates must have the flexibility to work nights, weekends, and holidays as part of a rotating schedule to ensure 24/7 fraud monitoring and response. This is essential to maintaining Ramp’s commitment to protecting its customers and minimizing risk around the clock.

What You Need

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in fraud prevention or investigations

  • Experience within consumer/corporate/small business cards, payments, invoices, lending, or related industries

  • Excellent collaboration, written and verbal communication skills

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with NACHA rules and regulations

  • Experience with card network rules and regulations, including dispute and chargeback processes

  • Experience with funds recovery processes, including hold harmless letters and ACH recalls
